articles.title: Plotting your shampoo schedule around workouts and dinner plans? Welcome to 'hair wash math.'
articles.summary: Women are sharing their “hair wash math” on social media — the calculations behind timing shampoo days around workouts and nights out. Dermatologists have th...
articles.body:
Wash your hair today and tomorrow's hot yoga class will ruin it. Wait until after your class and you'll have greasy hair at dinner tonight. Wash it twice? Sure, but then you'll have to double up on your whole washing-and-styling routine, which no one wants to do.

Now, this surprisingly complicated calculation has a name: "hair wash math."

Content creator Julie Kahut perfectly captured the thought process in her YouTube short : "Me debating whether I really need to wash my hair... If I wash it now, I have to wash it again after I go to the gym in two days. But I want clean hair when I go out tomorrow night. So, do I wash it now and wash it again later, or leave it greasy for a day?" As another creator put it, it can feel like an " eternal struggle ."

Blogger Kerry Schicker of Jacksonville Mom handles it by mapping out her hair-washing schedule every week. "I will plan out on Sunday what days I'm going to wash my hair based on days I'm in the office, have a work dinner or happy hour with friends, am volunteering in my son's class, or something to do where I can't show up with my hair looking a mess," she wrote.

For some, the mental gymnastics can feel like yet another annoying item on their to-do list. As one person joked on Instagram : "Studies show that the mental load a woman carries about hair wash timing would break a man."

But here's one less thing to stress about: Dermatologist Dr. Joshua Zeichner , director of cosmetic and clinical research at Mount Sinai Hospital, tells Yahoo that there aren't many hard-and-fast rules for when — or how often — you need to wash your hair. Instead, how frequently you suds up depends on your hair type and your scalp. People with thick, curly or coily hair, who tend to have a drier scalp, for example, can get away with washing their hair less frequently than people with oilier scalps who have thinner, less dense hair.

Dr. Samila Asad, a dermatology and trichology specialist at The Female Health Doctor clinic, tells Yahoo that attending a sweaty workout class doesn't necessarily mean you need to wash your hair immediately after. You can, she says, let your sweaty hair dry rather than hopping in the shower. "You don't need to sacrifice every blow-dry just because you've had a workout," she says. "If you're not sweating that much and your scalp feels comfortable, there's no odor, there's no itching, it doesn't feel oily — you could just put a shower cap on and have your regular shower, and off you go."

After exercise or other sweat-inducing activities, let your scalp dry rather than immediately tying up sweaty hair. "When you do that, you can get more sweat buildup, and that plugs the follicles, so it prevents [hair] from growing properly," Asad says.

And while it's OK to skip a wash day after a workout, if you have flaking, itching, redness or other signs of inflammation, it may be time to properly clean your hair. This is especially true if you extend your hairstyle by using styling products like dry shampoo, which absorb some of the oils but don't actually cleanse the hair.

Going too long between washes can also contribute to dandruff. Zeichner explains that oil buildup can allow yeast to flourish on the scalp, triggering inflammation and those annoying flecks of dead skin.

The one time you really should not skip washing your hair is after swimming in a pool or the ocean. "If you go into a pool, it's either going to be salt or chlorine," says Zeichner. "And you are going to want to remove that, especially if you have color-treated hair" or blond hair, since chemicals in some pools can tinge hair green .

Bottom line: "The reality is that we need to maintain a basic level of hygiene," Zeichner says, "but the frequency of hair washing really depends on your hair type and personal needs and preferences."

articles.title: The remarkable rescue of a teenager trapped in Westhumble cave
articles.summary: After the incident, Fred Topliffe lived an accomplished life which included more cave exploration.
articles.body:
When a teenager went to a chalk cave to hunt for fossils, little did he know he would become part of a remarkable chapter in a Surrey village history.

The Westhumble cave, located in the North Downs near Dorking, was once mined for its chalk.

In February 1954, four adventurous youngsters - including Fred Topliffe - from London wanted to explore the site.

Pete Brown, from Dorking Museum, told Secret Surrey that the 15-year-old was interested in geology.

"He and his friends came well-equipped with helmets, torches and boots," he added.

"While they were exploring, they suddenly heard a rumble and the whole cave roof collapsed."

Brown said Fred was nearly completely covered and could only move his fingers and toes.

According to Dorking Museum, Fred's helmet protected his face.

Brown said one of the boys ran to the nearest village for help.

Police and fire service arrived, but there were initial challenges in rescuing the teenager.

"They were digging from the side but it became difficult because more rocks kept dropping," Brown said.

"The operation had to be paused because Fred was in great danger.

"Emergency services went to the top and found a way to dig in vertically."

Brown said there was even discussion about amputating Fred's leg at one point.

However, one firefighter named Bert Bullett found a way to free the youngster and volunteered for the most dangerous part of the mission.

According to the Mickleham Magazine, Bullett had spent nearly two hours dangling upside down and clearing the rubble from Fred.

"Bullett managed to pull the piece of chalk that was over Fred's leg and hauled him out," Brown said.

For his bravery, the firefighter was awarded the British Empire Medal.

Fred, who is now 88-year-old and lives in Oxfordshire, recalled: "The moment I feared I might not get out was immediately after the collapse.

"Once the rescue operation began, I felt much more confident that I would be rescued."

Despite his terrifying experience, he continued to be involved in cave exploration.

He was a co-founder of the Chelsea Speleological Society, one of the country's top caving groups.

Fred later joined the British Antarctic Survey on Signy Island, where he worked as a meteorological observer and studied snow petrels and Weddell seals.

"One of my proudest achievements is climbing out of a deep crevasse unaided in the Antarctic," he said.

When asked why he enjoyed cave exploring, he said he "couldn't explain the appeal", comparing it with the desire some people have to climb mountains or venture into unchartered places.

articles.title: Why Did a California County Fine Them Over $1 Million for Someone Else's Code Violations?
articles.summary: A recent settlement crippled a local code enforcement scheme—and exposed the perils of turning petty violations into government revenue streams.
articles.body:
Humboldt County, California imposed over $1 million in fines on property owners for alleged cannabis code violations committed by the previous owner, leading to a settlement that wiped out the fines and required the government to provide due process.

The code enforcement scheme involved fines accruing at $12,000 per day, with property owners facing penalties for unpermitted development based on satellite images, even if they were not growing cannabis.

The plaintiffs, represented by the Institute for Justice, argued that the system violated their Seventh Amendment right to a jury trial, leading to a settlement that included sending warning letters before imposing penalties and holding hearings within 60 days.

Thanks to a settlement with several property owners, a wrecking ball is about to hit one California county's cannabis code-enforcement scheme—a system that piled ruinous fines on people for violations they say they did not actually commit.

Corrine and Doug Thomas, two of the plaintiffs, were staring down more than $1 million in civil penalties. That came with a twist. Humboldt County, California, said their property's previous owner, Summerville Creek LLC, had been in "violation of the commercial cannabis land use ordinance," had constructed "a building or structure in violation of building, plumbing, and electrical codes," and had "facilities or activities in violation of the commercial cannabis land use ordinance." The Thomases did not understand why that was their problem, having purchased the property once their home in Los Angeles County was destroyed by a wildfire.

Nevertheless, they were greeted with the news six days after moving in. Per county policy, fines accrued at $12,000 per day, for up to 90 days—and that included while people waited for the opportunity to have a hearing, which could take years. In the couple's case, they had the option to demolish the structure the government had deemed problematic, though that also would have cost them about $180,000, plus fines and fees.

How was the government getting this information? "Code-enforcement officers scour [satellite] images for what looks like unpermitted development on a property (e.g., a greenhouse, a building, a graded flat of land, or trees removed without a permit on record)," attorneys for the Institute for Justice (I.J.) wrote in a petition to the U.S. Supreme Court. "The County then presumes, without any evidence or further investigation, that the landowner must have developed their property without a permit because they were growing cannabis. In Humboldt's view, there's just no other reason that someone might not buy a permit before building a shed, a barn, or a greenhouse in the rural countryside."

I.J. represented several other plaintiffs in the case. One is Blu Graham, who waited four and a half years for a hearing to show he was growing vegetables (as opposed to cannabis) in his greenhouse. Another is Rhonda Olson, who faced $7.4 million in fines that were addressed to the previous owner on a property she purchased for $60,000.

The Court declined to hear the petition, which argued the plaintiffs had a Seventh Amendment right to a jury trial in such cases. (They instead had to fight the fines in administrative hearings conducted by the government, where their chances of success were predictably bleak.) But the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 9th Circuit kept the suit alive , on the grounds that the plaintiffs plausibly alleged the code enforcement scheme ran afoul of the Eighth Amendment's proscription against excessive fines.

After that, the county agreed to settle . Among the conditions of the agreement: In the future, the government must send a warning letter prior to imposing penalties, and provide due process—to include delaying fines until a hearing's conclusion and holding that hearing within 60 days. The plaintiffs' fines and fees were also wiped out.

The system was likely put in place, at least in part, to allow the county to cash in on cannabis after it was legalized. It is part of a broader pattern of local governments leveraging code enforcement to raise revenue. Sandy Martinez of Lantana, Florida, for example, owes the government over $165,000, plus interest, for such minor code violations as parking on her own grass . According to the state of Florida, that is not excessive.

articles.title: Akal Takht expels SGPC member Amarjit Chawla for allegations concerning ‘cardinal sin of adultery’
articles.summary: Akal Takht excommunicates SGPC member Amarjit Chawla and Golden Temple granthi Malkit Singh over rape/harassment allegations; barred for life from Sikh bodies.
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: The Akal Takht on Sunday excommunicated Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee (SGPC) member Amarjit Singh Chawla and Golden Temple additional head granthi Malkit Singh from Khalsa Panth over allegations of rape and harassment. Both have been barred for life from working in Sikh institutions.Akal Takht officiating Jathedar Kuldip Singh Gargajj, who is also the Jathedar of Takht Kesgarh Sahib, announced the decisions from the ‘faseel’ (podium) of Akal Takht following a meeting at its secretariat in Amritsar. The meeting included Takht Damdama Sahib Jathedar Tek Singh, Golden Temple granthi Kewal Singh, Akal Takht granthi Gurbakhshish Singh and one of the Panj Pyaras, Mangal Singh.Giani Gargajj said the allegations damaged the dignity of Sikh institutions. He cited the Panth-approved Sikh Rehat Maryada, which mandates excommunication for any of the four “Bajjar Kurehits“ (cardinal sins): dishonouring or cutting hair, consuming halal meat, adultery and tobacco use. “Chawla remains excommunicated until he proves his innocence and appears before the Akal Takht,” Giani Gargajj said.The action follows an Aug 21 FIR registered at Anandpur Sahib police station. A woman alleged Chawla raped her repeatedly between March and May at Anandpur Sahib and Amritsar after the SGPC provided her accommodation upon her Nov 2025 return to India. She also alleged Chawla threatened to kill her if she spoke out.Chawla denied the charges as a “completely false, baseless” conspiracy, but resigned from the SGPC and his post as Shiromani Akali Dal senior vice-president.The complainant also accused Malkit Singh and Takht Kesgarh Sahib driver Mohan Singh of sending her obscene messages. The SGPC suspended both on Sept 17. Though the FIR named only Chawla, the woman alleged misconduct by others.According to the FIR, the woman said she even approached Akal Takht Jathedar about the matter “several times” and “showed the proofs, but no action was taken”. Responding to a question on this, Giani Gargajj said, “I meet thousands of sangat (devotees) every day. That bibi (woman) met me in the same manner. She met me casually. She talked to me about Malkit Singh, mentioning that he did some inappropriate chat. She did not talk to me about Amarjit Singh or anyone other. She spoke to me verbally. Despite this, understanding my responsibility, I asked the Shiromani Gurdwara Parbandhak Committee to remove this man from the Akal Takht. And as far as I know, after that, he did not perform any service at the Akal Takht Sahib. If the woman had told me about Amarjit Singh, I would have taken strict action in the matter.”Announcing the excommunication of Malkit Singh, Akal Takht noted that when a person is serving in a responsible Sikh position, he carries a great responsibility towards the community and the religion to always maintain his character and moral conduct in accordance with the Guru’s teachings.” “The levelling of allegations against a person occupying such a responsible position brings collective dishonour to the community. Therefore, Malkit Singh is excommunicated from the Khalsa Panth. All Sikh sangats are directed not to maintain any kind of association with him. articles.title: Russia recruited Ukrainian children to carry out attacks. They were imprisoned.
articles.summary: KREMENCHUK, Ukraine - Yaroslav Suzanskyi was 16 when he saw an ad on the Telegram messaging app offering “easy money,” about $165, to do an odd job. It turne...
articles.body:
Russia recruited Ukrainian children to carry out attacks. They were imprisoned.

KREMENCHUK, Ukraine - Yaroslav Suzanskyi was 16 when he saw an ad on the Telegram messaging app offering "easy money," about $165, to do an odd job. It turned out to be a want-ad for sabotage: Suzanskyi was paid to set fire to a railway relay cabinet.

Now 18, Suzanskyi is incarcerated at a juvenile correctional colony, both a perpetrator and a victim of a hidden part of Russia's war against Ukraine: recruiting vulnerable young people to attack their own country. He is one of eight inmates at Kremenchuk - in a population of 72 - convicted of national security or public safety offenses linked to Russia.

Many of the children recruited by Russia are impoverished and are lured into betraying Ukraine with relatively small offers of money, the authorities said.

After torching the railway equipment, Suzanskyi got a bigger offer involving an explosive, for 60,000 hryvnias, or about $1,430. A man Suzanskyi knew as Artem sent him to a hotel in the Kyiv suburbs, where two backpacks were left outside Suzanskyi's room. One contained military clothing, the other a taped box with wires that Suzanskyi thought was a jammer but later learned was an explosive device.

He was then sent by taxi to a library. Ukrainian intelligence officers intercepted him there before he could complete the assignment.

"Those 60,000 turned into five years," Suzanskyi said.

Suzanskyi was 13 when Russia's full-scale invasion began. His father and stepfather were drafted, leaving his mother to support three children. A bureaucratic mistake stopped the family's child-support payments, and they fell behind on bills, he said. He began taking whatever work he could find.

In December 2024, with his younger brother's birthday and the winter holidays approaching, Suzanskyi said he had just 200 hryvnias, or about $5, left. That's when he responded to the ad on Telegram.

Across Ukraine, 13 minors are serving sentences in Russia-related cases, including five girls, according to the Justice Ministry. In all, more than 300 juveniles have been detained on similar charges, officials said. Some received probation, while others are still under investigation.

A report published last year by the Office of the U.N. High Commissioner for Human Rights noted "a surge in credible allegations that the Russian Federation used Ukrainian children in Government-controlled territory to conduct surveillance and transmit information on the Ukrainian military, or to commit sabotage and arson targeting military objects or public property with links to the military."

Russia denies the allegations and has blamed Ukrainian intelligence services for recruiting Russian minors to carry out sabotage in Russia.

Oleksii Babakov, now 17, spent about eight months under Russian occupation in Vovchansk, on the Russian border, where he was living in foster care. When he was 15, guardians helped get him to Kharkiv and eventually to live in Poland, which is when he saw a Telegram ad promising easy money.

Babakov was asked to recruit other young people and pass them on to a handler. One was Vikentii, now also 17, a friend of Babakov's from when they attended a cadet corps together in Kharkiv in 2022.

Vikentii spoke on the condition that he be identified only by his first name because of fear that he will be targeted for retaliation. Babakov told him that he could earn up to $3,000 a month.

At first, Vikentii said, he thought he would only have to make explosive devices. Later, he learned that he was also expected to plant one. He was 15 at the time.

He left the device in a trash bin outside a police station in Kharkiv and walked away. "When I blew up the bomb, I understood that I had done a really bad thing," he said.

He later saw a report that no one had been hurt. "I felt relieved," he said. "There'd been a terrorist attack, but no one was hurt."

From Poland, Babakov saw news reports about people he had recruited. One was Vikentii. Another was a 15-year-old girl who left an explosive device outside a different police station. No one was hurt in that blast either.

Ukrainian authorities tracked down Babakov in Poland, and he was deported to Ukraine. He and Vikentii met again in a pretrial detention center and are now serving their sentences together in Kremenchuk.

Vikentii was convicted of committing a terrorist act and sentenced to three years in prison. Babakov was convicted of inciting and assisting a terrorist attack and sentenced to four years.

Maksym Parshyn, 17, is from Slovyansk, in the eastern region of Donetsk that Russian President Vladimir Putin wants Ukraine to surrender.

Parshyn's mother has schizophrenia, and his family has struggled financially. Parshyn said legitimate employers were reluctant to hire him because he was too young. For a while, he loaded firewood and worked for illegal call centers scamming people in Russia.

"It's very easy," Parshyn said of finding work on Telegram. "You write something like 'find work,' and it's all there."

Parshyn accepted $300 from an anonymous Telegram contact he described as a "handler" to set fire to a railway relay cabinet. The next day, the same contact offered him more money to burn vehicles used by military recruitment officers. Parshyn said he refused and blocked the account.

A few weeks later, however, he accepted another offer to spray-paint graffiti on a military recruitment office. Months later, he returned to Telegram where a new handler had offered him $3,000 to set fire to a post office. Parshyn filmed while one of his friends set the fire.

Parshyn said he did not realize until he was detained that Russian intelligence services were using Telegram to recruit young Ukrainians for such attacks. He spent about a year in pretrial detention before being sentenced to four years.

"I needed money," Parshyn said. "If I hadn't needed it, I wouldn't have done it at all."

After turning 18, teenagers can remain in Kremenchuk for education and rehabilitation until age 22 or they may be transferred to adult facilities.

Deputy Justice Minister Yevhen Pikalov said the boys detained in Kremenchuk were motivated by money not treason.

"They did not do it with the motive of destroying the Ukrainian state," Pikalov said. "They didn't do it because they love Russia. $500 on Telegram, that's it."

In the colony, personal phones are not allowed. Staff hold the boys' SIM cards, and calls and video calls go through the institution.

Computers and tablets are supervised, and social media is blocked. During free time, the boys play sports, read, watch television or use a PlayStation. Money from family or earned inside the facility can be spent at the colony shop.

In Kremenchuk, as everywhere in Ukraine, life is overshadowed by Russian airstrikes.

Blast waves from nearby missile attacks have damaged the colony three times, but the detainees were in shelters, and no one was hurt, staff said. Air-raid alerts frequently interrupt classes at the school.

When The Washington Post visited on July 20, one room, normally used for table tennis, was set up for Ukraine's university entrance exam the next day. In another, chess and checkers boards came out. A few sat down to play while others chatted.

A key question for all of the boys is: What comes next?

Pikalov said that judging whether a youth has been rehabilitated depends on each teenager's risks and needs rather than the offense they committed.

Babakov dreams of a "clean slate." Parshyn said he wants to hug his family after getting out.

For Suzanskyi, that next step has already begun. He has started an online university degree in agronomy.

After turning 18 in June, Suzanskyi chose to transfer to a more restrictive medium-security prison for adult men, rather than remain in Kremenchuk.

"To try adult life," he said, "so I definitely won't want to end up in prison again." On Aug. 11, he left Kremenchuk.

With 3½ years still to serve, what worries him most is what might happen to his family as Russian attacks intensify.

"I'm afraid there simply won't be any relatives left by the time I get out," he said.

articles.title: Você sente culpa ao avisar no trabalho que está doente?  | G1
articles.standfirst: Até metade das pessoas no Reino Unido relata trabalhar mesmo estando doentes. Os motivos para isso são complexos, dizem especialistas.
articles.summary: Até metade das pessoas no Reino Unido relata trabalhar mesmo estando doentes. Os motivos para isso são complexos, dizem especialistas.
articles.body:
Você acorda se sentindo mal, mas tem um grande dia de trabalho pela frente.

O que você faz? Se a resposta for bater o ponto mesmo assim, você não está sozinho.

Pesquisas sugerem que entre um terço e metade das pessoas no Reino Unido trabalham mesmo quando estão doentes — algo que os especialistas chamam de "presenteísmo".

Por outro lado, gerações mais novas têm demonstrado maior preocupação com seu bem-estar, incluindo sua saúde mental.

Isso não quer dizer que a geração mais jovem seja "mimada", como frequentemente é rotulada, diz o professor Cary Cooper, psicólogo da Universidade de Manchester e um dos maiores especialistas mundiais em bem-estar no ambiente de trabalho.

"Talvez as gerações mais antigas tenham sido mais tolerantes [com a entrega incondicional ao trabalho], mas isso não significa necessariamente que essa escolha seja saudável", afirma Cooper.

"Quando se trata de fazer uma pausa, os trabalhadores mais jovens parecem mais dispostos a encarar o bem-estar mental como parte de sua saúde geral, em vez de algo que deva ser simplesmente ignorado."

A verdade é que a forma como você lida com problemas de saúde diz muito sobre você como indivíduo e sobre o lugar onde você trabalha.

Diversos fatores influenciam a forma como uma pessoa lida com o afastamento por doença.

Para alguns, o trabalho está intimamente ligado à identidade. Psicólogos organizacionais chamam isso de centralidade do trabalho — e pesquisas relacionam esse fato a um maior engajamento, comprometimento e disposição para se esforçar ao máximo.

Se o trabalho é essencial para quem você é, ausentar-se dele pode dar a sensação de perder temporariamente uma parte de si mesmo.

"Essas pessoas sentem um forte desejo de continuar comparecendo", explica Audrey Tang, psicóloga que escreve sobre bem-estar no local de trabalho.

De acordo com a especialista, aqueles que trabalham em profissões ligadas ao cuidado, como medicina, enfermagem e ensino, têm uma tendência a isso.

"Eles frequentemente relatam que preferem sofrer um acidente físico para ter uma justificativa para não comparecer ao trabalho, em vez de simplesmente tirar o dia de folga."

Outros temem ser vistos como fracos ou preguiçosos.

Os trabalhadores mais jovens são particularmente suscetíveis a essa pressão, diz Tang.

"É mais provável que estejam no início da carreira e não queiram causar uma impressão negativa."

O que isso diz sobre o lugar onde você trabalha

A cultura do ambiente de trabalho pode influenciar significativamente a disposição das pessoas em tirar dias licença por motivo de doença — Foto: Getty Images/Jacob Wackerhausen

Os padrões no ambiente de trabalho podem ter uma influência significativa na disposição das pessoas em tirar licença médica, afirma a psicóloga Tara Quinn-Cirillo.

Quando as equipes estão sobrecarregadas e há pouca ou nenhuma cobertura disponível, os funcionários sabem que sua ausência aumentará a carga de trabalho dos colegas.

"O papel da culpa e da vergonha é significativo em uma organização tóxica que prioriza a produtividade em detrimento da saúde e do bem-estar", aponta Quinn-Cirillo.

"Em alguns locais de trabalho, existe uma cultura de 'seguir em frente' que incentiva as pessoas a continuarem trabalhando quando deveriam estar descansando."

Esses ambientes de trabalho valorizam o presenteísmo. Os funcionários se sentem valorizados por comparecerem ao trabalho, independentemente de como estejam se sentindo.

Se os gestores elogiam a performance de algum empregado que está trabalhando doente, a equipe rapidamente assimila a mensagem.

"Em um ambiente de trabalho saudável, as pessoas devem poder ter conversas abertas e honestas sobre bem-estar e dias de licença médica", diz Quinn-Cirillo.

A confiança também é importante. Se a ausência for rotineiramente questionada ou vista de forma negativa, os trabalhadores podem ficar relutantes em fazer uma pausa por motivos legítimos, devido ao medo de serem julgados.

Segundo Quinn-Cirillo, isso é um "grande sinal de alerta".

Como saber se você está doente demais para trabalhar

Decidir se você está doente demais para trabalhar nem sempre é simples.

Para doenças físicas, Tang afirma que existem algumas regras bem estabelecidas.

"Se você estiver vomitando e tiver diarreia ou febre, deve ficar em casa por 48 horas e 24 horas, respectivamente, após o desaparecimento dos sintomas. Nessas situações, é improvável que você consiga trabalhar de forma eficaz de qualquer maneira."

De acordo com a psicóloga, há no entanto situações em que a decisão fica mais difícil, sobretudo quando o trabalho remoto é possível.

"No caso de tosses e resfriados, há uma zona cinzenta. Desde a covid-19, a etiqueta no ambiente de trabalho mudou — geralmente, é considerado mais educado trabalhar em casa."

Ela afirma ser imprescindível que a saúde mental seja tratada da mesma forma que a saúde física.

Quinn-Cirillo acrescenta: "Em última análise, trata-se da capacidade de realizar um trabalho, seja ela física ou mental."

Um outro sinal de alerta é quando o trabalho começa a afetar os cuidados básicos de saúde pessoal, diz ela.

"Sua capacidade de cuidar de si mesmo está mudando? Você consegue relaxar do trabalho? Seu sono está bom?"

Se a resposta for não, pode ser um sinal de que o repouso é exatamente o que você precisa.

articles.title: Gasolina com 35% de etanol pode estragar o carro? Veja peças que podem ser afetadas | G1
articles.standfirst: Governo autorizou testes para elevar dos atuais 32% para 35% a mistura de etanol. Especialistas apontam maior preocupação com veículos antigos, mas modelos mais novos também podem sentir efeitos.
articles.summary: Governo autorizou testes para elevar dos atuais 32% para 35% a mistura de etanol. Especialistas apontam maior preocupação com veículos antigos, mas modelos mais novos também.
articles.body:
Carros que não são flex podem sofrer com aumento da mistura de etanol na gasolina — Foto: Marcelo Camargo/Agência Brasil

O governo autorizou o início dos testes que aumentam a mistura de etanol na gasolina comum, chegando a 35% — atualmente são 32% na bomba do posto.

Ainda há etapas a serem cumpridas antes de o combustível chegar aos postos com a nova mistura. Mesmo assim, a medida já levanta questionamentos sobre possíveis danos a peças e motores , especialmente os projetados para rodar apenas com gasolina.

Especialistas ouvidos pelo g1 foram unânimes ao afirmar que a nova composição da gasolina afeta de maneira mais direta e intensa os carros antigos. Ainda assim, os modelos mais novos também podem enfrentar problemas.

Entre os principais efeitos na direção estão o aumento do consumo de combustível e a redução da autonomia dos veículos movidos exclusivamente a gasolina.

"Quanto mais etanol for adicionado à gasolina, maior a dificuldade de queima ideal do combustível, porque a compressão do motor não é o bastante para o melhor aproveitamento do combustível e a temperatura de trabalho dos carros a gasolina, são inferiores aos carros flex ou a álcool", aponta Tenório Júnior, técnico e professor de mecânica automotiva.

🔎 A taxa de compressão indica o quanto o motor comprime a mistura de ar e combustível antes da combustão que movimenta o veículo. Uma forma simples de entender é imaginar uma mola: quanto mais ela é pressionada, mais força libera ao ser solta. Os motores projetados para funcionar com etanol trabalham com níveis mais altos de compressão, enquanto a gasolina suporta índices menores.

“Isso [a taxa de compressão incorreta] gera falhas, perda de potência e dificuldade nas partidas a frio”, diz Tenório.

O especialista afirma que os problemas são os mesmos já apontados para a atual mistura de 32% de etanol na gasolina, "porém, um pouco pior" .

Partes afetadas pelo aumento de etanol na gasolina

Carburador aberto com corrosão (parte áspera e clara) por etanol — Foto: Bruno Bandeira/arquivo pessoal

Carburador: presente apenas em veículos mais antigos, anteriores à popularização da injeção eletrônica nos modelos zero-quilômetro, é o componente que mais preocupa os mecânicos. “Os carburadores são ‘burros’. Eles não se adaptam ao combustível. Nos carburadores, a passagem de ar e de combustível para obter a mistura ideal é fixa”, diz Tenório. Além de prejudicar o desempenho do motor nos veículos mais antigos, Bruno Bandeira, mecânico e proprietário da Oficina Mecânica Na Garagem, afirma que o carburador pode sofrer corrosão com o aumento da concentração de etanol na gasolina. “Esse material não foi feito para suportar etanol, então olha o que está fazendo. Esse carburador tá condenado”, diz Bruno.

Tanque de combustível: o problema também se concentra nos carros mais antigos, especialmente aqueles equipados com tanque metálico. Nesses casos, a peça pode precisar ser substituída. Segundo os três mecânicos ouvidos pela reportagem, os tanques de plástico, presentes na maioria dos veículos lançados desde o início dos anos 2000, não apresentam a mesma preocupação.

Bomba de combustível com corrosão pelo etanol — Foto: Bruno Bandeira/arquivo pessoal

Bomba de combustível: o etanol presente na gasolina pode conter até 0,7% de água. No entanto, Alexandre explica que, se o veículo permanecer parado por muito tempo, o combustível tende a absorver a umidade do ar, aumentando a quantidade de água na mistura. Essa água acelera o processo de corrosão da bomba de combustível. Segundo Bruno, os danos também podem atingir a boia responsável por indicar o nível de combustível no tanque.

Bicos injetores (de injeção direta ou indireta): segundo os especialistas, os veículos sem turbocompressor tendem a ser os mais afetados por esse tipo de desgaste. “A central aumenta o tempo de injeção para compensar o menor poder energético do E35. Se os bicos já estiverem parcialmente sujos, o aumento da demanda pode deixar o problema mais evidente, causando falhas ou marcha lenta irregular”, diz Alexandre.

Velas de ignição com corrosão pelo etanol — Foto: Bruno Bandeira/arquivo pessoal

Velas de ignição: s egundo os mecânicos, o problema costuma surgir apenas quando as velas já estão desgastadas. Alexandre explica que, nesses casos, elas podem contribuir para falhas na queima do combustível, já que o motor exige uma regulagem mais precisa da mistura.

Catalisador: sua vida útil pode ser reduzida quando ele recebe combustível que não foi queimado corretamente, o que pode ocorrer devido a uma mistura inadequada dentro do motor.

Mangueiras, retentores e itens de vedação: em veículos mais antigos, esses componentes podem ressecar e se desgastar mais rapidamente.

"Se continuar aumentando a porcentagem, logo esses carros a gasolina não conseguirão andar sem fazer uma série de adaptações", aponta Tenório.

Alexandre Dias, mecânico e proprietário das oficinas Guia Norte, explicou que, em carros sem carburador, a ECU, também conhecida como módulo de injeção eletrônica, pode ser atualizada para que o motor se adapte à nova proporção de etanol na gasolina.

Ele também destacou que uma manutenção mais cuidadosa dos componentes citados anteriormente pode ajudar a preservar a durabilidade do veículo.

Já nos modelos mais antigos, Tenório afirmou que é possível adaptar o carburador, embora o processo esteja longe de ser simples.

Segundo ele, a dificuldade aparece “porque tem furos de passagem de ar e de combustível (giclês) no carburador, que são substituíveis por serem peças de rosca, mas será necessário ir ajustando e testando para ver o resultado, porque não existe uma tabela com as aplicações para esse tipo de combustível”.

articles.title: Extrema direita alemã diz ser 'partido do povo' e prevê queda de Merz | G1
articles.standfirst: AfD venceu eleições regionais em Macklemburgo-Pomerânia Ocidental, o 2º estado a obter supremacia da ultradireita em menos de um mês. Resultados dos pleitos colocam governo federal de Friedrich Merz em xeque.
articles.summary: AfD venceu eleições regionais em Macklemburgo-Pomerânia Ocidental, o 2º estado a obter supremacia da ultradireita em menos de um mês. Resultados dos pleitos colocam governo federal de Friedrich Merz em xeque.
articles.body:
Chanceler da Alemanha, Friedrich Merz, em reunião de seu partido União Democrática Cristã (CDU) em 21 de setembro de 2026, um dia após eleições regionais 'desastrosas'. — Foto: REUTERS/Fabrizio Bensch

Após nova vitória da AfD em eleições estaduais na Alemanha , a copresidente do partido de extrema direita Alice Weidel afirmou que sua sigla "já substituiu" a CDU —partido do chanceler Friedrich Merz — como "partido do povo".

“A AfD é claramente o novo partido do povo na Alemanha . Superamos a CDU e as pessoas querem uma mudança política”, afirmou Wiedel em entrevistas na TV alemã no domingo após seu partido vencer as eleições reginais em Mecklemburgo-Pomerânia Ocidental, o 2º triunfo da extrema direita em um mês.

Um outro dirigente da Alternativa para a Alemanha (AfD) disse nesta segunda-feira (21) que o chanceler conservador deixará o poder até o fim do ano por conta de derrotas da CDU em eleições regionais.

"O crepúsculo do chanceler [Merz] começou" , declarou Leif-Erik Holm, candidato da AfD em Mecklemburgo, que venceu as eleições de domingo com 38% dos votos.

Merz afirmou no domingo que ele pretende continuar no poder e prometeu reformas na Alemanha para impedir novos avanços da extrema direita. No entanto, o chanceler reconheceu que a situação não é boa para seu governo e chamou as eleições em Mecklemburgo e em Berlim de "desastre".

A União Democrata-Cristã (CDU), de centro-direita, obteve apenas 4,9% dos votos em Mecklemburgo, abaixo do limite de 5% necessário para entrar no Parlamento regional. Este é o pior resultado da sigla em eleições regionais desde a fundação do partido em 1945.

A CDU também perdeu votos nas eleições estaduais em Berlim, que inclui a capital alemã, e foi superada pelo partido de extrema esquerda Die Linke, enquanto a AfD obteve avanços significativos na capital.

articles.title: Anvisa manda apreender lotes falsificados de remédio contra câncer e toxina botulínica  | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida atinge unidades de um lote do Phesgo que exibem data de fabricação falsa e três lotes do Dysport que não são reconhecidos pela fabricante. Resolução foi publicada nesta segunda-feira (21).
articles.summary: Medida atinge unidades de um lote do Phesgo que exibem data de fabricação falsa e três lotes do Dysport que não são reconhecidos pela fabricante. Resolução foi publicada nesta segunda-feira (21).
articles.body:
Phesgo, remédio contra o câncer, tem versão falsificada circulando no mercado — Foto: Roche

A Agência Nacional de Vigilância Sanitária (Anvisa) determinou a apreensão de unidades falsificadas do medicamento contra o câncer Phesgo e da toxina botulínica Dysport . A decisão foi publicada no Diário Oficial da União desta segunda-feira (21).

No caso do Phesgo, a medida vale para unidades do lote B5011B05 que apresentam junho de 2025 (06/2025) como data de fabricação.

Segundo a Anvisa, a Roche, responsável pelo registro do medicamento, informou ter identificado no mercado unidades desse lote com características diferentes das do produto original.

A agência determinou a apreensão e proibiu o armazenamento, a comercialização, a distribuição, a importação, a exportação e o uso das unidades falsificadas.

O Phesgo é um medicamento biológico usado no tratamento de determinados casos de câncer de mama HER2-positivo.

Dysport, toxina botulínica — Foto: Reprodução

A Anvisa também determinou a apreensão de três lotes falsificados do Dysport 500 U, medicamento à base de toxina botulínica tipo A.

P22368, com validade em fevereiro de 2029.

Segundo a resolução, a Beaufour Ipsen Farmacêutica, responsável pelo registro do Dysport, informou à agência que não reconhece esses lotes como originais.

Com isso, a Anvisa proibiu a comercialização, a distribuição e o uso dessas unidades.

As medidas têm caráter preventivo e entraram em vigor nesta segunda-feira (21). O g1 procurou a Roche e a Ipsen para saber quais orientações devem ser seguidas por consumidores, pacientes e serviços de saúde que tenham adquirido unidades dos lotes falsificados. A reportagem será atualizada quando houver retorno.

articles.title: Trump diz que promove ataque às 'fake news': 'Devem ser detidas' | G1
articles.standfirst: Presidente dos EUA baniu CNN, MS NOW e Politico, que produzem jornalismo consolidado e cobertura crítica a seu governo, de entrarem na sede do governo. Agora, chamou as 'fake news' de ameaça à segurança nacional do país.
articles.summary: Presidente dos EUA baniu CNN, MS NOW e Politico, que produzem jornalismo consolidado e cobertura crítica a seu governo, de entrarem na sede do governo. Agora, chamou as 'fake news' de ameaça à segurança nacional do país.
articles.body:
O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, fala com repórteres antes de embarcar no Air Force One na Base Aérea Conjunta Andrews, em Maryland, em 9 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Foto de BRENDAN SMIALOWSKI/AFP

Em meio a uma polêmica com a imprensa dos Estados Unidos , o presidente Donald Trump afirmou nesta segunda feira (21) que seu governo promove um ataque às "fake news", que chamou de uma ameaça à segurança nacional do país.

Trump afirmou que as fake news "crescem como um câncer" nos EUA e "precisam ser detidas".

"A Casa Branca não está promovendo um ataque à imprensa livre, algo que eu valorizo. Ela está promovendo um ataque às FAKE NEWS, algo que cresceu como um câncer em nossos amados Estados Unidos da América. Elas são corruptas, intencionais, disseminadas, totalmente coordenadas e completamente fora de controle. São uma ameaça à nossa segurança nacional e precisam ser detidas, AGORA!", afirmou Trump, em sua rede social Truth Social.

A fala de Trump ocorreu em meio a uma polêmica com os jornais CNN, MS NOW e Politico, que foram banidos por ele de entrar na Casa Branca sob acusações de fabricar mentiras contra seu governo . No entanto, ele não apresentou provas para sustentar sua acusação.

Trump novamente deixou de dar exemplos sobre o que considera ser "fake news" e não citou nominalmente nenhum dos três veículos que ele baniu da Casa Branca, porém sua fala tende a escalar a polêmica porque desde que ele retornou à Casa Branca ele tem equiparado a mídia tradicional ao que chama de "fake news".

Os três veículos de comunicação costumam fazer uma cobertura mais crítica ao governo dos EUA, mesmo assim eles são conhecidos como tendo um jornalismo consolidado. Os jornais afirmaram que entrarão nesta segunda com um processo na Justiça contra o banimento do governo Trump.

Esta não é a primeira vez que Trump ataca jornais tidos como parte da mídia tradicional dos EUA ou que tenta dificultar o acesso de jornalistas à cobertura presidencial. Seu governo abriu espaço para veículos ideologicamente alinhados e também restringiu o acesso da agência de notícias Associated Press (AP) no ano passado.

Repórter da CNN faz transmissão ao vivo em rua de Washington, nos Estados Unidos, após ser impedida de entrar na Casa Branca por determinação de Donald Trump, em 19 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Anna Rose Layden/ Reuters

articles.summary: O Vestibular Cederj 2027.1 oferece vagas em cursos de graduação para polos como Angra dos Reis e Volta Redonda com inscrições até 29 de outubro.
articles.body:
O Cederj abriu as inscrições para o vestibular destinado ao primeiro semestre de 2027. Ao todo, são 2.016 vagas para cursos de graduação semipresencial para o Sul do Rio e Costa Verde. Os interessados podem se inscrever até o dia 29 de outubro.

As inscrições devem ser feitas no site da Fundação Cecierj. As vagas são para 12 cursos de diferentes modalidades.

De acordo com a organização, a prova conta com 45 questões de múltipla escola, que cobrem conteúdos do ensino médio como língua portuguesa e literatura, língua estrangeira, biologia, física, matemática, química, geografia e história e, redação com caráter eliminatório.

articles.title: Moradores relatam falta de água há seis dias em Teresina | G1
articles.standfirst: Empresa afirma que houve uma falha eletromecânica e informou que equipes atuam no local.
articles.summary: A falta de água em Teresina atinge o loteamento Nova Santana após falha eletromecânica, e a concessionária Águas de Teresina trabalha no reparo dos equipamentos.
articles.body:
Moradores do loteamento Nova Santana, e do Residencial Deus Quer, na Zona Sudeste de Teresina , relatam estar há cerca de seis dias sem água. Em nota, a Águas de Teresina informou que o abastecimento na região foi afetado por um problema eletromecânico.

Em vídeos enviados à TV Clube , moradores mostram torneiras sem água. Eles contaram que a falta de abastecimento tem prejudicado atividades básicas do dia a dia, como cozinhar, tomar banho e limpar a casa.

A concessionária afirmou que equipes trabalham para restabelecer o fornecimento de água o mais rápido possível.

Segundo a empresa, após a conclusão dos reparos, o abastecimento será retomado gradualmente.

Imagens enviadas à TV Clube mostram torneiras secas e baldes vazios — Foto: Reprodução

A Águas de Teresina informa que o abastecimento no Loteamento Nova Santana e no Residencial Deus Quer, na zona Sudeste da capital, foi impactado por uma ocorrência eletromecânica em um dos equipamentos que integram o sistema de abastecimento da região.

Equipes especializadas atuaram no local durante o fim de semana e conseguiram restabelecer a operação de um dos equipamentos. Nesta segunda-feira (21), os trabalhos seguem com prioridade para a conclusão do serviço no segundo equipamento, que permanece em manutenção.

A empresa está atuando para restabelecer o abastecimento na região o mais rápido possível. Após a conclusão do serviço, o fornecimento de água será retomado gradualmente, conforme a pressurização do sistema.

Em caso de dúvidas ou para registro de ocorrências, os clientes podem entrar em contato pelo 0800 223 2000, por ligação ou WhatsApp, disponível 24 horas, ou pelo Águas App.

*Juliana Cristina, estagiária sob supervisão de Lucas Marreiros.

articles.title: Jornais processam governo Trump após serem banidos da Casa Branca | G1
articles.standfirst: Veículos de imprensa anunciaram nesta segunda (21) ação na Justiça contra decisão do presidente dos EUA. Jornalistas foram barrados no final de semana. Veículos de comunicação costumam fazer uma cobertura mais crítica ao governo norte-americano.
articles.summary: Veículos de imprensa anunciaram nesta segunda (21) ação na Justiça contra decisão do presidente dos EUA. Jornalistas foram barrados no final de semana. Veículos de comunicação costumam fazer uma cobertura mais crítica ao governo norte-americano.
articles.body:
Repórter da CNN faz transmissão ao vivo em rua de Washington, nos Estados Unidos, após ser impedida de entrar na Casa Branca por determinação de Donald Trump, em 19 de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Anna Rose Layden/ Reuters

Os veículos jornalísticos CNN, MS NOW e Politico anunciaram nesta segunda-feira (21) que vão processar o governo Trump após terem sido banidos da Casa Branca.

“Nesta manhã, notificamos o governo de que estamos entrando com uma ação judicial hoje para proteger nossos direitos garantidos pela Primeira Emenda [da Constituição dos EUA] e defender o princípio de que o governo não decide o que a imprensa noticia ou publica”, disseram as três organizações de notícias em um comunicado conjunto.

“Sem aviso ou qualquer procedimento, a Casa Branca revogou as credenciais de nossos jornalistas porque se opôs às nossas reportagens. (...) Se não for contestada, essa medida ameaça a liberdade de imprensa e o direito do público a um jornalismo independente e livre de interferência do governo”, acrescentaram os veículos.

O processo ocorre após o presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, ter anunciado na sexta-feira que baniu os três veículos de imprensa de acessarem a Casa Branca e os acusou, sem apresentar provas, de fabricar mentiras contra seu governo. Os jornalistas que trabalham para essas organizações tiveram seu acesso negado já durante o final de semana.

Os três veículos de comunicação costumam fazer uma cobertura mais crítica ao governo dos EUA , mesmo assim eles são conhecidos como tendo um jornalismo consolidado.

Esta não é a primeira vez que Trump tenta dificultar o acesso de jornalistas à cobertura presidencial. No ano passado, a Casa Branca determinou que a agência de notícias Associated Press (AP) seria barrada de eventos no Salão Oval e de voos no Air Force One em retaliação à cobertura da AP sobre a mudança de nome do Golfo do México.

articles.title: Seleção de arquitetos prevê reconstrução de casas atingidas por chuvas | G1
articles.standfirst: Projeto Reconstruindo Lares conta com recursos de R$ 9,6 milhões para reformas em unidades habitacionais e intervenções em lotes que foram atingidos pelas chuvas de fevereiro. Profissionais autônomos, empresários individuais e empresas com apenas um sócio podem participar da seleção.
articles.summary: Projeto Reconstruindo Lares conta com recursos de R$ 9,6 milhões para reformas em unidades habitacionais e intervenções em lotes que foram atingidos pelas chuvas de fevereiro. Prof
articles.body:
Bairro Três Moinhos, em Juiz de Fora, seis meses após chuvas — Foto: Marcus Pena/TV Integração

Estão abertas as inscrições para o credenciamento de profissionais de arquitetura e urbanismo para atuação no projeto Reconstruindo Lares, em Juiz de Fora. A iniciativa prevê o atendimento de 192 famílias, com reformas em unidades habitacionais e intervenções em lotes que foram atingidos pelas chuvas de fevereiro na cidade .

Podem participar profissionais autônomos, empresários individuais e empresas com apenas um sócio. Os credenciados serão responsáveis pela elaboração de projetos arquitetônicos de melhorias em moradias e a emissão de laudos de conclusão das obras.

Os interessados podem se cadastrar pelo Portal de Chamadas Públicas do CAU/MG , onde também está disponível o edital com as regras da seleção.

A seleção é uma iniciativa da Prefeitura de Juiz de Fora (PJF) em parceria com o Conselho de Arquitetura e Urbanismo de Minas Gerais (CAU/MG)e o Ministério Público de Minas Gerais (MPMG). O projeto Reconstruindo Lares conta com recursos da ordem de R$ 9,6 milhões destinados pelo MPMG para a recuperação de moradias afetadas pelas chuvas na Zona da Mata.

Os profissionais habilitados serão classificados conforme a pontuação obtida no critério de qualificação profissional.

Entre os critérios previstos no edital está a atuação anterior no Projeto de Assistência Técnica de Interesse Público (ATIP) em Juiz de Fora ou Ubá.

Também somam pontos aqueles que comprovarem experiência em planejamento urbano, mobilização social, assistência técnica para habitação de interesse social (ATHIS) e/ou diagnóstico territorial em Juiz de Fora.

A classificação será feita a cada habilitação, considerando a documentação e a pontuação apresentada pelos interessados.

O CAU/MG é responsável pela elaboração e condução do edital de credenciamento e pela seleção dos profissionais. A supervisão técnica dos projetos ficará a cargo da Companhia Municipal de Habitação e Inclusão Produtiva (Emcasa).

Já a execução do Reconstruindo Lares será responsabilidade da PJF. O projeto também prevê acompanhamento social das famílias, elaboração de orçamentos, aquisição de materiais, contratação e execução das obras.

As famílias beneficiárias serão selecionadas a partir dos registros da Defesa Civil e da possibilidade técnica de recuperação dos imóveis . Também serão considerados critérios socioeconômicos, como a inscrição no Cadastro Único (CadÚnico).

articles.title: Chuva e ventos fortes no RS: Defesa Civil e Inmet emitem alertas | G1
articles.standfirst: Formação de frente fria e baixa pressão causam instabilidade no estado. A partir de terça-feira, massa de ar polar avança e derruba temperaturas, que podem chegar a 2°C na Serra e na Campanha.
articles.summary: Formação de frente fria e baixa pressão causam instabilidade no estado. A partir de terça-feira, massa de ar polar avança e derruba temperaturas, que podem chegar a 2°C na Serra
articles.body:
A segunda-feira (21) começou com temporais em diferentes regiões do Rio Grande do Sul . Por volta das 2h50, a Defesa Civil estadual enviou um alerta vermelho por meio do sistema Cell Broadcast para moradores de Porto Alegre e da Região Metropolitana . O aviso previa "tempestades com rajadas de vento acima de 90km/h".

Em São Jerônimo, as rajadas chegaram a 115,8 km/h. Em Rio Grande, o vento foi de 113,7 km/h. Em Cerrito, foi de 104,1 km/h. Pelo menos 20 cidades tiveram rajadas de vento acima de 80 km/h, conforme a Climatempo Meteorologia.

Na Região Metropolitana de Porto Alegre, há estragos em Nova Santa Rita, Novo Hamburgo, Canoas e Eldorado do Sul.

A Defesa Civil organiza uma força-tarefa para retirar os entulhos das ruas e dimensionar os prejuízos.

articles.title: Handsworth baby bank helping more parents in full-time work
articles.summary: The couple who run the bank say they are in "desperate need" of baby formula as demand is so high.
articles.body:
A Birmingham baby bank says it is helping a growing number of people in full-time work who are struggling to afford essentials for their children.

Kavita Kaur Dhillon and her husband Karvinder run the Handsworth Baby and Family Bank on Soho Road, which provides free items including nappies, baby formula, clothes and toys.

The couple said the majority of people they first helped were from low-income households, but they were now seeing more working families needing support with everyday costs.

"We don't need any more clothing, it's the everyday essentials, formula, nappies, wipes, toiletries," said Kavita.

Karvinder said demand had shifted in recent years.

"Before, we mainly needed nappies," he said.

"As the daily cost of living has gone up, people need help with more day-to-day things."

The couple said they were currently in desperate need of baby formula and often had only a handful of tubs left in stock.

"Just because you dress nice, or drive a nice car, doesn't mean you don't need help," Kavita said.

"Nobody knows people's circumstances. People can judge, but the reality is people are struggling."

The bank, which operates from inside the couple's Dhillons Boutique store, has been helping families since 2024.

Kavita believed sharing a space with the shop helped remove some of the stigma that can come with asking for support.

"You go out of our shop and people think you have purchased something, but in fact you've just used our baby bank," she said.

She described it as a "warm and welcoming space" and said demand had continued to grow since it opened.

For the couple, supporting families remains the most rewarding part of the project.

"For me it is fulfilling, knowing I've been able to support or help someone else be okay and smile," Kavita said.

She urged anyone who was struggling not to suffer in silence.

"It's nothing to be ashamed of or to be scared of. There's no shame in asking for help."

articles.title: Mystery of who must pay to fix Stratford-upon-Avon sculpture
articles.summary: When large-scale public art is damaged, whose job is it to fix it - and will anyone step forward?
articles.body:
Two months ago, a major piece of public art was badly damaged in a car crash.

The Armillary Sphere sculpture still stands in the centre of the roundabout at the junction of Banbury Road and Trinity Way in Stratford-upon-Avon, but its steel is bent and twisted.

It is in need of fixing. Or, its critics say, in need of taking away.

The thing is, it is unclear which - if any - of those options will happen. No-one will take responsibility for the future bill as mystery surrounds who is in charge of the artwork's upkeep.

As several councils deny it is down to them to solve, one former mayor has suggested the piece was unwanted from the start.

It was put up 15 years ago using part of a £100,000 pot given by local housing developers for public art projects but proved controversial, with a petition to remove it getting 1,183 signatures in 2009.

Former mayor Cyril Bennis said he wants to see the damaged sculpture removed.

"It's a love-hate relationship I have with this," he said. "Most people in our community don't like it.

"The bottom line will be, it's got to be removed. It will cost more money to fix this mangled mess of steel."

Warwickshire County Council is responsible for the safety of local roads but told the BBC that it had "no involvement in the commissioning, delivery or installation of this sculpture.

"The responsibility for this is with Stratford District Council under their 2005 Arts Strategy."

Stratford District Council confirmed it was "currently investigating the circumstances surrounding the damage".

It said it was also "exploring the options available for repairing or reinstating the sculpture" and was "seeking to recover the associated costs from the insurer of the vehicle involved in the incident".

But it added none of that meant the district council had responsibility for the structure.

It is not clear whether any report was ever made to Warwickshire Police about the crash, or whether the driver had been identified.

Meanwhile, Stratford Town Council said none of its records showed it had ownership of the piece.

It seems, for now at least, the only thing that is certain is how much Bennis dislikes it.

Bennis has campaigned to get the statue removed since it was first conceived.

"This was not the way to encourage people how to understand art" he said.

"It's a lump of steel and it's just rusting, rusting for the last 20 years."

He said he wanted to see a line drawn under the affair and money raised from scrapping it, spent on the town.

"Thank God it is 100% recyclable because hopefully, if we get it recycled, if we get it pulled down, taken away... then the money can go towards potholes."

articles.title: How climate change is reshaping Britain's trees
articles.summary: Hotter summers are forcing growers to rethink which trees thrive in the UK.
articles.body:
One of the UK's biggest tree nurseries says it is already changing the species it grows as hotter, drier summers reshape conditions for growers.

Frank P Matthews, based in Tenbury Wells, Worcestershire, produces more than a million trees every year, supplying garden centres across the country.

After what it describes as a challenging growing season, the family-run business has introduced new drought-tolerant species, reduced water use and adapted the way it irrigates its trees.

Managing director Stephanie James said growers had little choice but to adapt to a changing climate.

"We've phased out some species that aren't doing so well and introduced others that thrive in hotter conditions," she said.

Among the varieties now being grown are cercis, lagerstroemia and koelreuteria, which are better suited to warmer weather.

The nursery captures rainwater and stores it in large lagoons, providing a vital supply during dry spells.

"We wouldn't be able to grow trees like this if we didn't have them," James said.

The business has also begun using a compost additive that reduces water consumption by about 30%.

"It means the water doesn't run through the pots quickly. It spreads horizontally and takes its time," she said.

Container-grown trees are watered using drip irrigation systems that deliver small amounts of water regularly to keep compost moist while minimising waste.

Elsewhere on the site, bare-root trees are grown in fields and irrigated using water extracted under licence from a nearby river. When water levels fall below a certain point, irrigation stops and the nursery relies on the resilience of the trees themselves.

As well as adapting to changing conditions, the nursery says diversity will be increasingly important as the UK's treescape evolves.

"If you look around the country, a lot of the ash are dying," James said.

"We need to keep replanting new and diverse species.

"The key to mitigating climate change from a tree point of view is planting a wide range."

The nursery, which grows around 2,000 different species, is encouraging people to plant trees as part of National Tree Week in November.

Despite this summer's dry conditions, James said autumn remains the best time to plant because roots have time to establish before the following growing season.

Her advice for gardeners is simple: use plenty of bark mulch.

"Mulching is very key to reducing water loss and helping to protect that root system," she said.

articles.title: London museum bosses warn against charges for overseas tourists
articles.summary: The government said it would explore charging international visitors to enter national museums.
articles.body:
Charging overseas tourists to visit London's museums could harm the capital's cultural appeal and put institutions at risk, museum bosses have warned.

Mayor of London Lord Sadiq Khan has opposed government plans to consider charging international visitors at national museums, saying that free museums and galleries were a "fundamental" part of London life.

A government spokesperson said no decisions had been made and an update was expected in the coming months.

The proposals come as rising costs and lower-than-expected visitor numbers fuel concerns about the future of museums, with sector leaders describing the current climate as "very challenging".

In March, the government said it would explore charging international visitors to enter DCMS-sponsored national museums in England as it looks for ways to tackle funding pressures.

Free admission has been in place since 2001 at the UK's 15 national museums, including 12 in London, for both domestic and foreign visitors.

Speaking to the London Assembly's Economy, Culture and Skills Committee on 9 September, Sir Tristram Hunt, director of the Victoria & Albert Museum, said he was "yet to be convinced of the benefits" of charging overseas visitors.

"It will affect our business model of not charging people at the door but in the café, gift shop, exhibitions and membership," he said.

"That would be scuppered by charging. We are at risk of falling back relative to the US and Europe."

There were also concerns around the ethics of a commercialised museum model.

Rebecca Pullen, chief of staff at Imperial War Museums, said that the institution's role "was to be there for everyone", adding: "Anything that impedes that is difficult for us to think about."

While the proposed charges would apply only to national museums, the debate came against a backdrop of wider financial pressures across the museum sector.

Pullen said the sector faced a "very challenging" financial climate, citing real-terms cuts to DCMS funding, visitor numbers that remain below pre-pandemic levels, and lower spending in museum cafes and gift shops amid the cost-of-living crisis.

Director of the Art Fund, Jenny Waldman, said "museums have very high fixed costs to care for their collections and keep their doors open".

She added: "Most of our museums have found a way of increasing their income through commercial and earned income but that has not kept pace with energy costs and National Insurance contributions."

In recent months City Hall has called on ministers to fund London's museums at levels comparable to European counterparts.

In July, deputy mayor for culture Justine Simons said the mayor had invested more than £800m in culture during his 10 years in office and that City Hall was working to support the sector.

"We cannot rest on our laurels. The UK is the lowest funder of the arts in Europe at a national level. Times are challenging. We have all got to work together to protect, grow, sustain our creative offer," she said.

A spokesperson for the government's Department for Media, Culture and Sport (DCMS) said: "We know introducing international charging would be complex and there are many practical and financial considerations.

"No decisions have been taken and we will provide an update later this year."

articles.title: 'Ted Lasso has changed my life,' says Oxford City goalie
articles.summary: Oxford City goalkeeper Robyn Cullen plays a recurring character in the fourth series of the TV show.
articles.body:
"Ted Lasso has literally changed my life."

Robyn Cullen usually plies her trade as a goalkeeper in the fifth tier of English women's football, but is now making as much of a name for herself away from the pitch.

The 19-year-old Oxford City player features as a recurring character in the latest series of Apple TV's Ted Lasso - playing a goalkeeper named Robyn.

Series four of the hit show sees Jason Sudeikis' eponymous American manager take control of fictional club AFC Richmond's new women's team.

"When the first episode that I was in came out, our living room was full," Cullen said.

"My mum has watched it so many times - she watches each episode by herself first, then with me or my dad and then again by herself in the evening.

"She just can't believe it, it's very cute."

Cullen began her football career at Chelsea, then moving to Wycombe Wanderers, before ending up at Oxford City this summer.

It was a family friend working in the TV industry that first suggested she expand her horizons, and audition to be a background actor for the latest series of Ted Lasso.

"My mum's friend basically said: 'I know what this is casting for, get Robyn to go for it because it will be an absolute laugh, and she might get it, she might not'," Cullen said.

"Obviously, I'm a Ted Lasso fan so I went for it and I thought 'this is hilarious, there is no way this is ever going to happen'.

"So I sent in my headshots and some videos of me playing football and then I just kept getting callbacks. I was so confused."

Fast forward and Cullen found herself on set alongside the show's stars - including Sudeikis, Hannah Waddingham and Brett Goldstein.

"I came in as an extra just on the football team, and I was not meant to be in many scenes - just the background and football stuff," she said.

But in the first week, an injury to an actor playing a more prominent member of the team gave Cullen the chance to step into the role.

"They asked me to take her place, so I then moved up and all of a sudden it got very real and then there were loads of cameras and I was on Ted Lasso.

"I was absolutely over the moon," Cullen, who features in every episode of the series, bar the first, said.

She said the writers based the characters "off of ourselves" for the "core eight" members of the on-screen team.

"Each one of the core eight kept our own names and then had a play on our last name - so I was Robyn Batman," she said.

The 10-episode series comes off the back of a major increase in the exposure of, and participation in, women's football - both in the UK and across the globe.

"It's absolutely amazing, I feel so grateful to be able to be a part of that," Cullen said.

"I've seen how women's football has taken off over the years, obviously, as a player myself... this is us, this is what we can do and we are important.

"It's just so lovely for people to be able to see that and so lovely for that to be celebrated especially by a network as big as Apple TV."

Looking to the future, Cullen said she would hopefully be back on the pitch for Oxford City "soon" following a recent injury, before hinting that a return to the fictional pitch at AFC Richmond might also be on the horizon.

articles.title: India-Japan air exercise Veer Guardian signals growing strategic alignment in the Indo-Pacific
articles.summary: News News: The successful conclusion of Exercise Veer Guardian 2026 has once again put the spotlight on just how far the India-Japan defence relationship has com.
articles.body: The successful conclusion of Exercise Veer Guardian 2026 has once again put the spotlight on just how far the India-Japan defence relationship has come, evolving from routine military exchanges into a genuinely comprehensive strategic partnership spanning operational cooperation, defence technology, maritime security and emerging military capabilities.This latest edition carried added weight because Japanese fighter aircraft operated from Indian soil for the very first time, a genuine milestone in the growing military engagement between the Indian Air Force and the Japan Air Self-Defense Force. Beyond the air combat drills, the exercise served as a visible demonstration of the trust, interoperability and strategic convergence steadily building between two of the Indo-Pacific's most important powers, both of whom share overlapping concerns about regional security.JASDF Chief General Takehiro Morita flew a sortie in a twin-seat variant of India's indigenous Tejas Light Combat Aircraft, calling it a symbol of India's technological innovation, a clear signal of Japan's appreciation for the country's growing aerospace capabilities. IAF Chief Air Chief Marshal AP Singh, for his part, led a Tejas formation flight during the exercise, underscoring both his own confidence in the indigenous platform and just how operationally mature the aircraft has become.For New Delhi and Tokyo, Veer Guardian represents far more than an air force engagement, it's one visible piece of a defence relationship that has expanded considerably over the past decade. Air Chief Marshal Singh's description of Japan as an "Apatsu Mitram," a friend in times of crisis, captured the level of strategic trust now underpinning bilateral ties. Both nations are Quad members, sharing a commitment to a free, open and rules-based Indo-Pacific, an outlook that has steadily translated into deeper cooperation across all three services. Apart from Veer Guardian, the armies of the two nations conduct Exercise Dharma Guardian, while the navies regularly engage through JAIMEX and the multilateral MILAN exercise.This growing military relationship rests on a series of agreements signed, covering defence cooperation and exchanges, equipment and technology transfers, protection of classified military information, and a Reciprocal Provision of Supplies and Services agreement, all of which have collectively enabled smoother logistics support and interoperability.Defence technology cooperation has also gained real momentum, with the two countries signing their first joint defence equipment project in 2024 an agreement to co-develop the UNICORN mast system for the Indian Navy's warships. The mast integrates radar and communication antennas into a single structure that reduces a warship's radar signature while improving efficiency, thus making the vessel a more effective combatant.Japan's transport aircraft and maritime patrol platforms an be another area of common interest for India. This opens up genuine opportunities for co-development and co-production under the Make in India framework, potentially letting Japanese firms tap into India's manufacturing ecosystem for both domestic and export markets.The recent visit of Japanese Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi added further weight to this trajectory. In talks with Defence Minister Rajnath Singh, the two sides signed a Memorandum of Arrangement on maritime security cooperation, focused on maritime domain awareness, information sharing, and humanitarian assistance and disaster relief. Discussions also touched on mine countermeasures, shipbuilding, reciprocal ship repair facilities and joint defence research.The dialogue has even extended into next-generation technologies, with India examining pathways for future combat aviation capabilities, and reports suggesting discussions around potential Indian participation in Japan's Global Combat Air Programme, its sixth-generation fighter initiative. This programme is still at the exploratory stage and India is also in talks with France over the Future Combat Air System platform.Exercise Veer Guardian stands as a clear marker of a partnership that is increasingly operational, technology-driven and strategically significant. As both India and Japan deepen military cooperation amid a shifting Indo-Pacific security landscape.

articles.title: Does more funding mean rural buses are back in business?
articles.summary: A rise in bus miles with council funding might be starting to reverse the reduction in services.
articles.body:
Council-funded rural buses described as a "lifeline" by some are enjoying a resurgence after years of decline and new laws are giving authorities more power. Does this mean buses are back in business?

Government data shows council support for local buses is rising. With the exception of London, 17% of bus miles travelled across England were supported financially by government.

That's down from almost a quarter in 2010, with bigger drops in rural areas, but it is up from a pre-pandemic low of 13% in 2019-20.

However, fewer of us have been catching the bus.

Journeys per person in England stood at 88 in 2010 and that number was down to 63 by 2024-25.

Numbers dropped sharply during the pandemic and a recent rise has not returned them to pre-Covid levels.

Figures for 2024-25 show the councils providing the most support to their bus networks tended to be in rural areas.

The charity Bus Users UK described supported bus services as "fundamental to social inclusion" and "a lifeline, not a choice" for many.

"Without them, people can become isolated and less able to participate fully in their communities," a spokesperson said.

The council is one of those across the country attempting to tackle this using DRT - demand responsive transport.

It is a type of on-demand service that passengers book in advance when it is needed and the bus route changes depending on where people need to go.

In 2021, the Department for Transport provided £20m to 15 local authorities in England to trial DRT via the Rural Mobility Fund.

The Wiltshire Connect service has been rolled out in different areas across the county.

It has 13 minibuses operating across three zones and first launched in 2023.

There have been 250,000 journeys since, a spokesperson for Wiltshire Connect said.

Councillor Martin Smith, the cabinet member for transport in Wiltshire, explained it has been more "affordable" for the council.

"If we weren't doing this we'd be trying to subsidise a lot of rural bus routes taking very, very few people from place to place and here we have a solution where it's a couple of buses which move around the area all the time," he said.

People book via an app or over the phone and the cost is the same as an ordinary bus service.

Passengers have the option to be picked up from various spots close to them and travel to areas within a certain zone.

The council still subsidises other services, which are contributing to their supported mileage rather than the DRT.

It was expected at first that older people would mostly use DRT but the council said it had found younger people "piling in there".

Smith said: "If we can get the younger generation used to using public transport then they will continue to do that potentially through their adult lives."

One passenger, Cat Jones, and her family started using the service when they moved from London to Wiltshire.

They had not needed a car at their previous home and they said the buses were a "lifesaver".

She said: "In Wiltshire, you sometimes need more flexible transport than the scheduled buses allow and that's what Wiltshire Connect is.

"Everybody is smiling. You feel plugged into the community."

James, who is a Wiltshire Connect driver, said: "They [the passengers] love it.

"It's a service that has helped so many people be able to get out.

"I think some of them feel quite trapped, especially in the smaller villages."

Bus Users UK has described the overall mileage increase as "encouraging".

A spokesperson said: "It shows targeted investment can work but mileage alone does not tell the full story.

"A bus service is only useful if it enables people to make the journeys that matter - whether that is getting to work, attending a hospital appointment, accessing education or staying connected with friends and family."

It emphasised that the decline before the pandemic was down to local council budget cuts forcing them to "abandon" routes.

It said that to get people confident in using the bus again, long-term funding for networks "that people could rely" on was needed.

The Campaign for Better Transport said that the publication of a national bus strategy in 2021 had made "the value of buses more explicitly understood and authorities have had the option to step in and plug gaps in provision thanks to dedicated government funding".

Silviya Barrett, of Campaign for Better Transport, said: "It is great news that these services are now increasing but overall bus provision is still at a lower level than in 2010 and our mapping shows that many areas still do not have the bus service they need."

The Local Government Association has a similar view.

It described the recent investment in services as "good" but said it also wanted to see "sustained levels of funding" to encourage people to use buses.

The government announced more funding last year as well as the Bus Services Act which gives local authorities more power over the buses in their area.

It is not just rural council-backed services that have shrunk.

The miles on the buses - for commercial routes too - have been slowly dropping since 2010. There has been a drop of about 22% since 2010.

It is back on the rise but has yet to reach the same levels as pre-Covid.

Commercial bus miles decreased by a quarter between 2010 and 2025.

The government's own analysis shows that some change in mileage between commercial and supported might be down to post-pandemic changes.

Companies, for example, may have stopped non-viable services, with local authorities helping fund the routes instead.

The Confederation of Passenger Transport (CPT) said one of the reasons is bad traffic.

Worsening congestion on the roads has made buses slower and therefore less attractive to passengers. It can also make them pricier to run.

The organisation said buses outside London currently travelled on average at 11.7mph.

It said council support was needed most in rural areas, with lower populations making it harder to cover cost through bus fares and the countryside meaning "longer distances, more fuel".
