articles.title: US and China discuss AI safety plan ahead of Trump-Xi summit
articles.summary: Top US and Chinese officials held talks in New York on Sunday ahead of a Trump-Xi summit this week.
articles.body:
Top US and Chinese officials have discussed creating a new "notification mechanism" for AI incidents that could affect national security, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent told reporters on Sunday.

Bessent made the comments after what he called "successful" talks with Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng in New York.

The meeting came as US President Donald Trump and his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping are due to hold a summit in Washington later this week.

AI has come under intense scrutiny in recent days after researchers warned of the potential risks posed by the technology and some of the industry's most high profile figures called for developers to take a more cautious approach.

"We think that, just like with any cross-border activity, that moving from opaque to more transparency between the number one and the number two AI powers in the world is very important," Bessent told reporters after the talks.

He said the meeting also covered other topics, including plans to "operationalise" a process to identify potential tariff cuts on goods called the Board of Trade.

A truce in the tariffs war between the world's two biggest economies is due to expire on 10 November.

The BBC has contacted the Chinese embassy in the US for comment.

Chinese state news agency Xinhua said the two sides had "candid, in-depth and constructive exchanges on key economic and trade issues", noting that they had discussed AI.

Bessent said in a post on X on Sunday that the talks "help lay the groundwork for President Trump to advance America's economic interests and deliver results for the American people."

The US and China are locked in a race to dominate the AI and technology industries.

In recent days Washington has faced calls to slow down the development of AI over fears abouts its potential negative impact on humanity.

Trump has largely dismissed those concerns , arguing that there are sufficient policies around AI and that the US cannot lose its edge to China.

He said earlier this month "whoever wins in AI, wins."

In May, when Xi hosted Trump in Beijing, ways to collaborate on AI was one of the issues the two leaders discussed.

Those talks ended with an agreement that China would buy Boeing jets and US agricultural goods in exchange for lower tariffs.

articles.title: Ethiopia conflict: Seven armed groups form alliance against Abiy Ahmed
articles.summary: The groups have been active in Ethiopia's most populous regions for years and now say they will work together.
articles.body:
Several of the rebel groups which have been fighting the Ethiopian authorities in different parts of the country have announced they have formed an alliance to remove the government in Addis Ababa.

The alliance brings together the Fano militia in Amhara, the Oromo Liberation Army (OLA), Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and four other smaller groupings in a coalition named Alliance for Survival.

The seven groups accuse Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government of presiding over "war, genocide, mass destruction, and utter poverty", claiming Ethiopia is at risk of disintegration.

The BBC has asked the government for comment.

Ethiopia has faced years of armed conflict in Oromia and Amhara, the most populous states in the country.

There have also been renewed tensions in the northern Tigray region, where a two-year civil war left hundreds of thousands dead and displaced millions.

An African-Union peace deal ended that war in 2022, but there have been fears of a return to a full-scale conflict, with both sides accusing each other of violating that agreement.

Besides Oromia, Amhara and Tigray, the new alliance also includes groups based in three other regions - Somali, Afar and Benishangul-Gumuz – making up a half of Ethiopia's 12 regional states.

The states are structured largely based on their dominant ethnic groups – a system of ethnic federalism that gives some autonomy to the states, but which can present social and political challenges for the country which has more than 80 ethnic groups.

Some of the rebel groups in the new alliance have previously fought against each other but they say they will now work together against their common enemy.

Abdikadir Addaani Hirmooge, the spokesman for the Ogaden National Liberation Front (ONLF), which is part of the alliance, told the BBC that the government had not respected a peace deal signed in 2018 to end the conflict in the Somali region.

Addaani accused Abiy's Prosperity Party of being an "obstacle to the people" and "unleashing" wars and many deaths.

"Ethnic conflict, insecurity, and mutual oppression and pushing each other aside have not been eradicated, resulting in a need that has affected every ethnic group," he said.

Addaani said the groups in the new coalition were working to bring together communities that have been divided against one another.

"Our objective is for the communities to have democracy and to exercise their right to self-determination, to genuinely govern themselves," he said.

Amhara's Fano group fought alongside federal forces against the TPLF during the Tigray war.

It however turned against the federal government in an armed insurgency less than a year after the war ended, after refusing government orders to disarm.

The government has been fighting the OLA since 2018.

The announcement of the Alliance for Survival coalition comes months after reports of an alleged alliance between TPLF and neighbouring Eritrea.

Abiy responded by saying he had faith in Ethiopia's "defensive capabilities".

"Even if others were added, we do not have an iota of fear regarding Ethiopia's sovereignty," he told lawmakers in July.

The country held a general election in June, with Abiy's Prosperity Party retaining its overwhelming parliamentary majority, despite the poll being overshadowed by conflict, accusations of repression and little participation by opposition parties.

The Fano and OLA rebel groups rejected the election and its results.

The Tigray region and its six million inhabitants were completely excluded from the poll.

articles.title: A Florida music hall that hosted Louis Armstrong and Ray Charles closed in 1968; after a four-year, $4.8 million renovation, St Petersburg has reopened it
articles.summary: US News: St Petersburg’s historic Manhattan Casino reopened on Saturday, 58 years after it closed, following a four-year renovation of the 101-year-old buildin.
articles.body: St Petersburg’s historic Manhattan Casino reopened on Saturday, 58 years after it closed, following a four-year renovation of the 101-year-old building. According to St Pete Catalyst, the city has spent $4.8 million on the two-storey property, which will now operate as a rentable event space in the Deuces neighbourhood.Built in 1925 by Black businessman Elder Jordan, the venue was originally known as the Jordan Dance Hall and served as a major entertainment centre for the city’s African American community. It hosted live dance music on weekends and gospel performances on Sundays. The building also became a venue for proms, graduations, pageants, parties and conferences.Its upstairs music hall later became known for performances by some of the biggest names in American music. Louis Armstrong and his band performed there three times. Other musicians who appeared at the venue included the Count Basie Orchestra, Ella Fitzgerald, Ray Charles, B B King, Little Richard, Etta James, Sam Cooke, Muddy Waters, Bo Diddley and Otis Redding.The venue’s Black legacyThe Manhattan Casino was part of The Deuces, a business district that became an important centre for St Petersburg’s African American community during segregation. The venue was also part of the Chitlin’ Circuit, a network of Black-owned venues across the southern United States where Black musicians could perform.The building became especially active during the 1940s and 1950s. Along with visiting performers, it had its own house band, while jazz and swing groups from other parts of the country regularly played for community dances.The history of the building was reflected upon during the reopening. St Petersburg Poet Laureate Denzel Johnson-Green recited his poem, “The Get Down, the Boogie, and the Hope of Sweat”, describing the sounds that once came from the venue.The venue eventually closed in 1968. Several efforts were later made to remodel and revitalise the property, but those attempts did not result in its reopening.Renovation brings new lifeThe latest project has transformed the historic building into a city-owned event space. The two-storey structure covers 12,000 square feet and is located at 642 22nd Street S.The renovation included changes to both floors. A new first-floor event space was added, along with a conference room, green room, bar and kitchen.The second-floor music hall and ballroom, where many of the famous performers once appeared, also received upgrades. The floors were refinished, the ceiling was raised and new drapery was installed.The restored Jordan Ballroom now forms part of the event space. It is the same upstairs room associated with performances by Armstrong, Fitzgerald, Charles and King, among others.A new mural by artist Egypt Hagan has also been added to the property, giving the renovated building a new visual feature while retaining its connection with its past.A new community spaceSt Petersburg Mayor Ken Welch said the renovated building is intended to serve different groups in the community.“This is a totally different model. It’s a community event space that can serve so many constituencies. I think that’s the right model at the right time," Welch said at the event.Welch also said the reopened Manhattan Casino would serve as an anchor for the development of The Deuces and the nearby Warehouse Arts District.For Welch, the reopening also marked the return of a building that has remained part of the city’s history despite being closed for decades.“History does matter, St. Pete,” Welch said during the ceremony. “And so, after four years of renovations, we get to open these doors once again, and begin a new chapter for the Manhattan Casino.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Singapore is paying citizens to read books for 15 minutes a day: The initiative aims to curb doomscrolling and rebuild reading habits
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Singapore has introduced a national reading initiative that encourages citizens to spend at least 15 minutes a day reading, with virtual rewards offer.
articles.body: Singapore has introduced a national reading initiative that encourages citizens to spend at least 15 minutes a day reading, with virtual rewards offered for qualifying sessions. The ReadSG Challenge, organised by the National Library Board (NLB), uses gamification to encourage consistent reading and make books part of everyday routines. Participants can earn virtual coins through the CrowdTaskSG platform, with reports stating that each qualifying session earns 20 coins. The five-year movement comes as officials highlight concerns about excessive short-form digital content and the importance of sustained reading. Through daily targets, reading streaks and additional incentives, the initiative seeks to encourage long-form reading and foster a stronger reading culture across Singapore.Singapore's 15-minute reading challenge aims to curb doomscrollingThe National Library Board has introduced ReadSG as a five-year national movement to encourage Singaporeans to make reading a daily habit. The initiative comes amid concerns about changing reading patterns in an increasingly digital environment, where short-form content competes for people's attention. Its ReadSG Challenge uses the government-run CrowdTaskSG platform to encourage participants to log at least 15 minutes of reading each day. Qualifying sessions earn virtual coins that can be exchanged for cash-valued rewards. Rather than simply promoting reading as a leisure activity, the campaign aims to encourage sustained engagement with books and develop a long-term reading culture. The NLB says reading can strengthen focus, critical thinking and imagination, while the challenge uses small daily targets to make the habit easier to establish.What is the ReadSG Challenge?The ReadSG Challenge is one of the initiatives under Singapore's five-year national reading movement, launched by the National Library Board on 6 September 2026.The challenge runs on CrowdTaskSG, a government digital platform that allows users to complete activities and earn rewards. Participants can log their daily reading sessions and collect virtual coins as they work towards building a consistent reading habit.The programme includes personal goal-setting, reading streaks and experience points. The NLB's wider ReadSG movement aims to promote reading as a lifelong habit and establish a shared reading culture.How citizens earn virtual coins for readingParticipants can earn 20 virtual coins for each qualifying reading session of at least 15 minutes. Only one session can be logged per day, and users declare their reading activity through CrowdTaskSG.The reported conversion rate is 1,000 virtual coins for S$1. This means each qualifying session is worth two Singapore cents in cash-valued rewards.Participants must complete 50 sessions to accumulate 1,000 coins. The financial incentive is modest, with the challenge primarily designed to encourage regular reading rather than generate income.Why Singapore wants people to read moreThe NLB has raised concerns about the way people consume information in the digital age. The organisation has pointed to the abundance of short-form content and the challenge of maintaining deeper engagement with longer texts.Melissa Tam, chief executive of the NLB, said that people can scroll through hundreds of headlines, watch videos or obtain summaries of information. She explained that the 15-minute reading target is intended to encourage small, consistent actions that can develop into lasting habits.The organisation describes reading as beneficial for focus, critical thinking, imagination and making sense of the world. These are the campaign's stated objectives and claimed benefits, rather than outcomes that have already been demonstrated through an evaluation of the ReadSG Challenge.How gamification encourages reading habitsThe ReadSG Challenge incorporates game-inspired features to make daily reading more engaging. Participants can set personal goals, maintain reading streaks and earn experience points as they complete activities.The programme also includes redeemable virtual coins and other incentives. These features are intended to encourage people to return to the challenge regularly and track their progress over time.The NLB's approach focuses on making reading manageable by setting a daily target of 15 minutes. The aim is to encourage consistency rather than require people to spend long periods reading from the beginning.Read for Good links reading with charitable causesAlongside the reading challenge, ReadSG includes a charitable initiative called Read for Good, previously known as Read for Books.The programme encourages participants to read for 15 minutes a day while contributing towards charitable causes supporting communities such as kidsREAD and MINDS. The official ReadSG website lists Read for Good activities from 6 September to 7 October 2026.Read for Good is a separate charitable component of the broader reading movement. Its fundraising arrangements should not be confused with the virtual coins participants earn through the ReadSG Challenge.Singapore's five-year plan to build a reading cultureReadSG replaces the National Reading Movement and represents a new phase in Singapore's efforts to promote reading. The NLB launched the initiative during the country's inaugural National Reading Month.The wider movement includes activities designed to bring people together around books and reading. Its launch featured themed reading spaces, activity booths, a marketplace and a mass reading session at the National Library Building.President Tharman Shanmugaratnam attended the launch as guest of honour and serves as the campaign's patron. The NLB has also set a target of 150,000 sign-ups for its initiatives as an initial step in the movement.The NLB presents sustained reading as an activity that can support focus, critical thinking and imagination. These potential benefits provide part of the rationale for encouraging people to spend less time on rapidly changing digital content and more time engaging with longer texts.The ReadSG Challenge is designed to encourage a reading habit. Whether it produces measurable improvements in attention, critical thinking or long-term reading frequency will require evidence from future assessment.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: UK flight delays continue after issue with air traffic control in Scotland is resolved
articles.summary: Engineers are investigating the "technical issue" at the Prestwick Centre which handles air traffic control across Scotland and the north of England.
articles.body:
A "technical issue" with air traffic control in Scotland which has been causing delays to flights in the UK has been fixed, but disruption continues.

The national air traffic service (Nats) said engineers were called in to deal with the issue at the Prestwick Centre in South Ayrshire which handles air traffic control across Scotland and the north of England.

A spokesperson for Nats said the issue had now been resolved and they were working with airlines to safely lift air traffic regulations and minimise further disruption.

The service said the issue was not related to a software defect that led to the cancellation of 2,000 flights across the UK earlier this month.

Flights in Scotland, Northern Ireland and northern England disrupted by air traffic control issue

The Nats spokesperson said: "The issue in our Prestwick centre is now fixed. We are working with airports and airlines to safely lift air traffic regulations as quickly as we can to minimise any further disruption.

"Passengers should still check the status of their flight with their airline. We apologise for the disruption."

UK Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander posted on social media that the problems were "deeply frustrating for passengers after the previous issue".

Scotland's First Minister John Swinney said: "We'll engage with the national air traffic control service to ensure that these issues are addressed and that the resilience is necessary for these systems is available at all times."

Passengers have also taken to social media to confirm they are experiencing delays at Glasgow, Prestwick and Edinburgh airports.

Delays are also being reported at Manchester, Newcastle and Belfast airports.

The Manchester Airports Group said there have been delays of up to an hour on some flights at Manchester Airport and there are also delays at East Midlands Airport.

Several arrivals and departures at Belfast City Airport are cancelled, including flights to and from Manchester, Amsterdam, London City and, later on towards lunchtime, Glasgow and Edinburgh.

Dundee and Benbecula airports have also confirmed flights are impacted.

A spokesperson for Edinburgh Airport said: "We are experiencing some delays due to the Nats issue at Prestwick Centre.

"We are monitoring the situation closely and are working with Nats as they work to resolve the issue."

A spokesperson for AGS, which operates Glasgow, Aberdeen and Southampton airports, said: "Some services operating to and from our airports are experiencing delays, primarily at Glasgow Airport, and further disruption is expected due to the knock-on impact across the network.

"This is the second time in as many weeks that a Nats technical issue has had a significant impact on services operating through our airports, and we fully appreciate the frustration this will cause those whose travel plans have been disrupted."

A spokesperson for Highlands and Islands airports said flight schedules are being impacted across their 11 regional airports.

Ryanair said they had been notified of a Nats "equipment failure" affecting airspace above Scotland and northern England.

The airline said it was impacting flights to and from the UK and Ireland.

A Nats spokesperson earlier said: "Airports south of Manchester are broadly unaffected, however flights heading north and flights departing Scottish airports are currently subject to some delay."

Nicole McCloskey, from Kilmarnock, was due to be on a cancelled flight to Paris with her husband and daughters Aoife and Nuala.

She said: "We've rebooked another flight for this afternoon. Fingers crossed it's sorted in time.

"We were supposed to be going for four nights and going to Disney. Even if it is a shorter trip, we will get there."

Frank Bonner was due to be jetting off from Glasgow to Las Vegas to be best man at a friend's wedding but is now frantically trying to get another flight.

"It's our flight to London that's cancelled. We'll hopefully get there later but we're going to lose a day because the connection to Vegas won't be until tomorrow, we'll need a hotel tonight.

"The wedding is at the weekend but we had other plans like a helicopter ride that we won't make.

"Talk about best man nerves, I don't want to be having to deal with this."

Lewis Fraser from Inverness is on board a plane stuck on the runway at Glasgow Airport.

He told BBC News: "We boarded the flight as normal but were immediately told we were delayed.

"The latest update was around half an hour ago to say we might be waiting another hour and 45 minutes. Some passengers have left the plane in the last few minutes."

He is travelling to Heathrow to get a connecting flight to Chicago but said making his connection seemed "unlikely".

Airlines have expressed frustration at the problem which came just days after Nats published an initial report into a "software defect" which impacted air traffic control operations on 8 September.

Nats chief executive Martin Rolfe told BBC News he would not resign, saying the software defect was "very, very obscure".

Ryanair said the latest issue had impacted 140 of its flights and 25,000 passengers, and called on Rolfe to quit.

Ryanair's chief operations officer, Neal McMahon, said: "Just three days after Nats assured airlines and passengers that it had introduced robust 'mitigation plans', its flight data processing system has failed again.

"Martin Rolfe's report claimed that another failure was 'unlikely' and that Nats could recover more quickly if one occurred. Those claims have been exposed as completely worthless.

"Just three days later, passengers are once again suffering lengthy delays because Nats has failed to deliver either a reliable system or an effective back-up."

He called for Rolfe to resign or be removed from his position.

Steve Heapy, chief executive of Jet2, said customers being let down again was "simply not good enough".

He said: "Once again, airlines and customers are being disrupted by yet another Nats issue, and one has to ask: how many more failures do customers and airlines have to deal with.

"Customers work hard to look forward to their holidays, and airlines work hard to deliver those holidays. They should not be repeatedly exposed to delays and disruption because the UK's air traffic control systems cannot be relied upon."

British Airways said it was "disappointing" that some customers may experience disruption after "yet another technical fault with Nats".

Nats is the UK's leading provider of air traffic control services and handles about 2.5 million flights per year.

This is the fourth national air traffic incident in the past three years.

In 2023, a computer shutdown over the August bank holiday weekend caused chaos for 700,000 passengers.

There was another, smaller, Nats outage in 2025 which caused 150 cancellations.

articles.title: Meloni plans burqa, niqab ban in Italian schools; how it compares to rest of Europe
articles.summary: Europe News: Italy is preparing to ban the burqa and niqab in schools, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced on Sunday, putting the country back in the spotlight.
articles.body: Italy is preparing to ban the burqa and niqab in schools, Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni announced on Sunday, putting the country back in the spotlight of Europe’s long-running debate over face-covering veils, religious expression and integration.Meloni said her government would soon take a measure to the Cabinet that would prohibit burqas and niqabs in schools. She also proposed limiting the number of foreign students in each classroom and requiring parents of foreign students facing serious integration difficulties to learn Italian. The government has not yet specified the proposed limit on foreign students.“You must go to school with your face uncovered,” Meloni said, arguing that no one in Italy should be able to decide that a young woman must hide her face in the name of tradition. The proposed measure still needs to go through the legislative process before it becomes law.What exactly is Italy proposing?The proposal specifically refers to burqas and niqabs, but not hijabs. A burqa covers the entire body and includes a mesh covering over the eyes, while a niqab covers the face but leaves the eyes visible. A hijab covers the hair and neck but leaves the face uncovered.Italy already has a 1975 law restricting the wearing of clothing that makes identification difficult in public places. The issue of full-face veils has previously been dealt with under that framework in certain circumstances, but Italy has not had a nationwide law specifically banning burqas or niqabs in schools.The proposed school ban comes as Italy joins a wider European debate over how far governments can regulate face-covering clothing.How does Italy compare with the rest of Europe?There is no single European rule on burqas and niqabs. Countries have taken different approaches, from blanket public-space bans to restrictions in schools, hospitals and public transport, while some have no nationwide face-covering ban at all.France: It was the first European country to introduce a nationwide ban on clothing that conceals the face in public spaces in 2011. Violations can lead to a fine and, in some cases, a civic education course.Belgium: It was introduced as a nationwide ban in 2011. Violations can result in fines and prison sentences of up to seven days.Bulgaria: Full-face veils have been banned in public spaces since 2016, with wearing them restricted to private homes and places of worship.Austria: A nationwide ban on full-face coverings took effect in 2017. Austria has also gone further in schools: from September 2026, girls up to the age of 14 are prohibited from wearing Islamic headscarves that cover the head at school.Denmark: It introduced a nationwide ban on face-covering clothing in public places in 2018, covering garments including the burqa and niqab.Netherlands: Its 2019 law is narrower, restricting face coverings in places including schools, hospitals, government buildings and public transport rather than imposing a blanket public-space ban.Switzerland: A federal ban on face coverings in public spaces came into force in 2023 after voters approved the measure in a national referendum.Portugal: It completed legislation in August 2026 banning face coverings in public spaces, with exemptions including health, professional, artistic and religious settings.Germany: There is no nationwide blanket ban. Federal rules restrict face coverings in certain circumstances, including for some public employees, judges, members of the armed forces and motorists, while several states have additional restrictions.Sweden: There is no national ban on religious attire, although some municipalities have attempted school-level restrictions.Spain: It has no nationwide ban comparable to France's, with restrictions instead varying according to local or institutional rules.The European debate has therefore moved in different directions. France, Belgium and Denmark prohibit face coverings broadly in public, while countries such as the Netherlands limit them to specific settings.Italy's proposed measure is more narrowly focused on schools, putting it closer to Austria's approach than to Europe's blanket public-space bans. Whether it becomes law will depend on the legislative process that follows Meloni's Cabinet proposal.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Ekurhuleni killings: South Africa police arrest three over woman's body in Dawn Park
articles.summary: The body of Jabulile Ntimba was the ninth to be found recently in an area east of Johannesburg.
articles.body:
Three suspects have been detained in South Africa in connection with the murder of a woman in an area east of Johannesburg – the last of nine recent cases in that region that has shone a spotlight on the level of violence against women in the country.

Under pressure to solve the spate of murders which has involved victims' bodies being dumped on a roadside, police have described the arrests of the three – a man and two women - as a "breakthrough".

Referring to all nine cases, acting police chief Lt Gen Puleng Dimpane said her officers were "working tirelessly to bring those responsible to justice".

The three suspects are due in court on Monday.

Their case relates to the death of Jabulile Ntimba , whose half-naked body was found wrapped in a sheet in Dawn Park last Thursday.

Several of the recent victims were discovered partially clothed and with injuries, but police have stressed that they have not established whether all the deaths are connected or whether a serial killer is responsible.

Addressing journalists on Monday, deputy police chief Lt Gen Tebello Mosikili said that "a team of analysts are working hard to see if there are links to all these cases" but the killing of Ntimba "appears to be an indication of a murder that stemmed from a relationship... this includes... a possible love triangle".

South Africa has one of the highest rates of gender-based violence in the world. It also has a very high murder rate and though officials statistics do not identify the gender of the victims, a recent estimate from the country's Human Rights Commission indicated that, on average, six women were murdered every day between April and June this year.

The recent grim discoveries have sparked a national outcry about the scale of the problem and increased the feeling of insecurity for many women.

articles.title: Owaisi opens alliance door in UP; Congress warns AIMIM could end up helping BJP
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: With Uttar Pradesh gearing up for the 2027 assembly elections, Congress MP Imran Masood on Monday took a swipe at AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owa.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: With Uttar Pradesh gearing up for the 2027 assembly elections, Congress MP Imran Masood on Monday took a swipe at AIMIM chief Asaduddin Owaisi's alliance pitch, warning that the party's presence in the polls "would end up benefitting BJP."His remarks came a day after Owaisi said AIMIM was open to an alliance with "like-minded" parties seeking to prevent the BJP from returning to power in Uttar Pradesh for a third consecutive term.Speaking to ANI, Masood said, "If an alliance is to be formed, it should be finalised; otherwise, we must proceed with our own preparations. The political climate, not just here, but across the entire country, is such that one cannot move forward without the Congress; the Congress is essential. A fight against the BJP can only be waged with the Congress; only the Congress can take them on.""Rahul Gandhi's leadership is capable of overcoming them. Finalise it (alliance) immediately. I am not aware of who is in touch; I have no information regarding that so far. If it isn't finalised, the damage happens on the ground," he added.Responding to Owaisi's proposal, Masood said defeating the BJP was the primary objective but argued that strategic voting would be important."Defeating the BJP is the primary objective, and Muslims alone cannot defeat the BJP. If the BJP wins and forms the government, it is the Muslims who suffer the consequences. The political atmosphere in Hyderabad is different from that in Uttar Pradesh. Owaisi Ji might win 4-5 seats, but he ends up facilitating a BJP government. What will you do with those five MLAs? If a BJP government is formed, who suffers the loss? Since the BJP would form the government, people need to act sensibly. People must make decisions wisely and astutely," he said.Owaisi's alliance pitchOwaisi had earlier on Sunday said that AIMIM was ready to work with parties that share its objective of keeping the BJP out of power in Uttar Pradesh."We do not want the BJP government to be formed for a third time in Uttar Pradesh. If anyone does not want the BJP to form the government, they can talk to us. We are ready to work with you to stop the BJP from coming to power. But it is important to understand that you cannot stop the BJP alone," Owaisi said.Owaisi also cited AIMIM's experience in Bihar, saying the party had sought an alliance with opposition parties and asked for six seats, but the proposal was not accepted. He said AIMIM would continue building its organisation in Uttar Pradesh irrespective of alliance talks.Earlier in the day, Owaisi, meanwhile, said AIMIM was already preparing for the Uttar Pradesh elections and was hopeful of sending its candidates to the state Assembly."We are visiting specifically in connection with election preparations. Our party is fully prepared and actively gearing up; we are hopeful that this time our candidates will be elected as MLAs and enter the Uttar Pradesh Legislative Assembly," he said.On the possibility of an alliance, Owaisi said, "Wait until October 2nd; we will let you know by then."Akhilesh sets 27,000-vote targetThe Congress's push for an early alliance decision also comes as the Samajwadi Party steps up its preparations for the 2027 polls. At the party's state executive meeting on Sunday, Akhilesh Yadav said the SP would work to increase its vote share by 27,000 votes in every assembly constituency."Today was our state executive meeting. In this, we have decided that in the 2027 assembly elections, we will work to increase 27,000 votes in every assembly seat. That means we will reduce 27,000 votes of the BJP," Yadav said.Masood also criticised the Election Commission over Special Intensive Revision (SIR) notices, questioning the difficulties they could create for ordinary citizens."What could be more farcical in this country than a situation where Members of Parliament, former Chief Ministers, and even the External Affairs Minister receive such notices? If they are getting notices, the Election Commission's situation couldn't be more absurd. Imagine the plight of the common man or those who are unemployed and struggling just to find a single meal a day. Are they expected to run around with documents? Look at the state the country has been reduced to, constantly standing in queues. The system has failed. The system has completely collapsed," he said.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Calvin Harris recognised for 1.6m world record DJ set crowd
articles.summary: An estimated 1.6m people attended the Dumfries DJ's set in Sao Paulo in Brazil earlier this year.
articles.body:
Scottish DJ Calvin Harris has been celebrating writing his name into the record books after performing for an estimated 1.6m people in Sao Paulo earlier this year.

The musician from Dumfries received recognition from Guinness World Records (GWR) for the largest attendance for a DJ set by a single artist.

He took to social media to highlight the award for what he described as a "truly insane day" which he said could only have happened in Brazil.

GWR said it had been reported that his headline appearance had forced the closure of the Rua da Consolação with some fans fainting in the heat.

Harris has already been recognised for a number of other records in the past.

In 2014, GWR presented him with a certificate for most top 10 hits on the UK singles chart from one album for 18 Months which produced no fewer than nine.

It also lists him as the highest paid DJ in one year for his earnings between June 2015 and 2016.

GWR said Harris had turned Sao Paulo into "one massive street party" by climbing on board a carnival float for his performance on 8 February 2026.

Wearing a Brazilian football shirt with the name Calvinho on the back he worked his way through a setlist featuring many of his biggest hits.

The record book also noted that a similar-sized crowd attended Madonna's free concert on Copacabana Beach in May 2024 during her Celebration Tour.

articles.title: Onion packets weigh less than promised; consumer commission orders Rs 20,000 compensation
articles.summary: News News: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Punjab has directed a supermarket and its parent company to pay Rs 20,000 to a customer who was allegedly.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A district consumer commission in Punjab has directed a supermarket and its parent company to pay Rs 20,000 to a customer who was allegedly supplied underweight onion packets under a promotional offer. The commission found deficiency in service and unfair trade practice and passed the order on September 3, 2026.Why did the customer approach the commission?According to the commission order, Vikas Taluja visited the store in Ropar on April 25, 2026 and purchased goods worth Rs 3,299. Under an offer for customers shopping above Rs 999, he was allowed to buy two 2-kg packets of onions at Rs 9 per kg.Taluja alleged that when he checked the packets on the store's weighing machine, one weighed 1.788 kg and the other 1.784 kg. The total weight was about 3.574 kg instead of the promised 4 kg. He also submitted a video recording of the weighing.However, the supermarket claimed that there was no visible weight discrepancy when the packets were sold. It said the customer was later asked to bring the product to the store so that it could be physically verified and the issue resolved, but he declined and filed the complaint.What did the commission find?The bench comprising President Kuljit Pal Singh along with members Ranvir Kaur and Ramesh Kumar Gupta said the weighing was carried out on the store's own machine in the presence of its staff and that the video recording showed the customer informing the staff about the underweight packets.The commission said the store did not send a responsible officer to examine the complaint at the spot.“The weight of the two packets was measured by the complainant in the presence of the staff of the Ops on the weighing machine of the Ops in the store. In this regard, the complainant also relied upon the videography pen-drive Ex.C4, vide which he made the videography during the measurement of the onion packets,” the bench observed.The commission further relied on the video recording and said the customer had asked a responsible officer to witness the measurement, but no such officer came forward.“But despite it, no responsible officer of the store visited at the asking of the complainant to see the underweight packets supplied to the complainant. It further proved the negligence/deficiency in service/unfair trade practice of the OPs that no responsible person of the store made any efforts to resolve the grievance of the complainant at the spot,” the bench added.The commission held that the evidence showed that the customer received less quantity than what was mentioned on the packets and invoice. It said the supply of underweight onions amounted to unfair trade practice and deficiency in service.“Hence, we are of the considered opinion that underweight onion packets were supplied by the OPs to the complainant and it is unfair trade practice/deficiency in service on the part of the OPs,” the commission concluded.The complaint was partly allowed. The supermarket and its parent company were jointly and severally directed to pay Rs 20,000 as a lump sum towards compensation and litigation expenses within one month of receiving the certified copy of the order.The commission also directed that if the amount was not paid within the stipulated period, the companies would have to pay interest at 9 percent per annum on the Rs 20,000 amount until realisation.

articles.title: Tories pledge to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists
articles.summary: The party says scrapping the scheme in 2021 left the UK less competitive than European destinations.
articles.body:
The Conservative Party has pledged to bring back tax-free shopping for tourists from outside the European Union.

The Tories said the decision to scrap the scheme in 2021 left the UK less competitive than European destinations.

Leader Kemi Badenoch, who was a Treasury minister when the tax relief was abolished, said businesses were being "let down by a tax policy that is chasing their customers away".

But Labour accused the party of "a spectacular U-turn".

The VAT Retail Export Scheme - which allowed overseas visitors to get a VAT refund on items they had bought in Great Britain and took home in their luggage - was scrapped for non-EU visitors under the previous Conservative government in 2021, while it was also not extended for EU visitors.

At the time, Badenoch said it was "a costly relief which does not benefit the whole of GB equally".

However, the Conservatives have now set out plans to restore VAT refunds for eligible visitors from outside the EU.

The party said that if evidence confirms the scheme "pays its way", this would be extended to visitors from the EU by the end of the next Parliament.

It said the cost of reintroducing the scheme would be offset by cracking down on "NHS health tourism", including more consistent charging of patients ineligible for free treatment, minimum recovery targets for debts and requiring full repayment of debts before visa applications or renewals will be considered.

The remaining costs would be funded from a package of savings set out by the Tories last year.

Reinstate VAT-free tourist shopping, businesses say

Bring back duty-free perk to boost London - mayor

The party also argued the move would benefit shops, hotels, restaurants and the wider tourism industry.

It pointed to research by the Centre for Economics and Business Research (Cebr), which suggested fully restoring tax-free shopping for tourists could attract up to 2.35 million extra visitors and generate £4.1bn in extra spending.

The report from earlier this month also estimated that for every £1 of VAT refunded, this could generate £1.54 in other taxes.

Badenoch said: "We have iconic retailers, inventive designers and brilliant manufacturers, but they are being let down by a tax policy that is chasing their customers away.

"Holidaymakers are choosing rival cities in other countries for the simple reason that it saves them money."

Businesses have long called for tax-free shopping for tourists to be reintroduced, arguing they are at a disadvantage to other European countries.

EU countries offer VAT refunds for non-EU visitors, while other European countries such as Switzerland have similar schemes.

Helen Dickinson, chief executive at the British Retail Consortium, said: "Introducing a modern tax-free shopping scheme would help attract more international spending to the UK, supporting high streets, jobs and investment in towns and cities across the country.

"Done properly, it would boost economic growth and deliver a net benefit to the Exchequer."

However, a Labour spokesperson said: "Kemi Badenoch used to say tax-free shopping was a costly giveaway and now she's trying to sell it as an economic miracle.

"If they really think it's such a great idea, they should explain why they scrapped it in the first place and how they'd pay for bringing it back."

articles.title: Southport killer accused of throwing boiling water mixed with sugar at prison officer
articles.summary: Axel Rudakubana is accused of grievous bodily harm and two other assaults of prison officers while serving a life sentence.
articles.body:
Southport killer Axel Rudakubana has appeared in court accused of throwing boiling water mixed with sugar at a prison officer.

The 20-year-old is charged with the attempted grievous bodily harm of a prison officer at HMP Belmarsh, over allegedly throwing the boiling mix through the hatch in his cell door on 8 May last year.

He is also charged with two other assaults of prison officers, as well as possession of a knife or other offensive weapon while in prison.

Rudakubana, who is serving a life sentence for murdering three children at a dance class in Southport in July 2024, appeared via video link at Westminster Magistrates' Court wearing a tracksuit top.

He spoke only to confirm he could hear the chief magistrate, and to give his name and date of birth. He rested his head on his hand during the hearing.

Prosecutor Catherine Pattinson told the court prompt medical attention prevented the prison officer Rudakubana is alleged to have attacked on 8 May from suffering any lasting injury.

The prosecution also accused him of threatening to soak a female officer outside his cell if she did not pass him a newspaper on 6 May 2025, then throwing an "unknown liquid" at her through his door hatch.

Then, on 28 October last year, he allegedly punched a male prison officer in the face. The prosecution said the officer was trying to establish whether Rudakubana had taken his medication at the time.

The offensive weapon charge relates to sharpened stone shards that the prosecution say had seemingly been prised from the floor of the defendant's cell.

They were found stuck to the under side of a shelving unit in his cell. Pattinson told the court that "when questioned by a prison officer, he said that he was keeping them for self-defence".

Rudakubana, who appeared from Broadmoor secure psychiatric hospital, was not asked to enter pleas during the hearing on Monday. He was remanded into custody to appear at the Old Bailey on 19 October.

He is serving a life sentence for the murders of nine-year-old Alice da Silva Aguiar, six-year-old Bebe King, and Elsie Dot Stancombe, seven.

Rudakubana was also convicted of the attempted murder of eight other children and two adults during the attack in July 2024 at a Taylor Swift-themed dance class.

articles.title: Helen Jenner announced as new leader of Reform in Wales
articles.summary: Farage says it was "untenable" for former leader Dan Thomas to continue after his arrest last week.
articles.body:
Nigel Farage has unveiled Helen Jenner as the newly-elected leader of Reform in Wales, replacing Dan Thomas after his arrest on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour.

Speaking on the steps of the Senedd in Cardiff on Monday, Farage said: "I've known Helen for many, many years. She is a determined campaigner."

Farage said he was sorry for former leader Thomas's "personal difficulties" and that it had been untenable for him to continue, adding: "We could have done without this bump in the road."

Jenner, who served as Thomas's deputy alongside her role as Senedd member for Bangor Conwy Môn, said it was an honour to be elected to the top job.

A leadership vote was held by Reform's 33 Senedd members on Monday morning - Jenner confirmed that her colleague Jason O'Connell had stood against her. There was no vote of the wider party membership.

O'Connell had not been expected to stand.

Speaking to reporters outside the Senedd, Farage said there would be a vote for a new Welsh deputy leader to replace Jenner on Tuesday.

Jenner had been interim leader and favourite to replace Thomas, with sources telling BBC Wales that "very senior" Reform figures had backed her.

She is a married mother-of-two from Anglesey and had spent 15 years working as a teacher.

A fluent Welsh speaker, Jenner had been a member of all Farage's parties since UKIP, and stood for the Brexit Party in the 2019 Senedd election.

Thomas stepped down on 15 September after he was arrested on suspicion of assault and controlling or coercive behaviour. He was bailed pending further enquiries , and denies doing anything wrong.

He was not on the steps of the Senedd for Jenner's unveiling as leader, but he remains a Reform MS after chief whip Llŷr Powell said he had not considered removing the whip from him.

After he stepped down, Thomas had been among the Reform Senedd members who met in Cardiff Bay last week to discuss their next steps, with a party official from London attending to oversee proceedings.

Nigel Farage told reporters that it was "pretty much untenable for him to continue as leader".

He described Jenner as "someone I trust".

Farage added the party will carry on "as if nothing had happened, waiting for Dan, who is going to stay a member of this place, to come back more actively with us".

Speaking to BBC Wales, Jenner said there were a "few things" Reform needed to change, including giving members more of a say on policy.

She denied the party had a "unity issue" after James Evans claimed last week he would have had "majority" support to stand as leader had he not ruled himself out.

"I think that it was a really difficult time for us," Jenner said.

"They say a week's a long time in politics - to be honest, 24 hours was a long time in politics. But I think we are really united in terms of what we're trying to achieve here."

articles.title: BBC removes 11 Mitchell and Webb comedy sketches from iPlayer
articles.summary: The corporation said it had included "the ones that still work today and not the ones that don't."
articles.body:
The BBC has removed nearly a dozen comedy sketches from That Mitchell and Webb Look after deciding they no longer "work today".

The Bafta-winning comedy, written by and starring David Mitchell and Robert Webb, originally ran for four seasons between 2006 and 2010.

The show recently returned to the BBC's iPlayer to mark its 20th anniversary. But 11 old sketches, including one that reportedly showed the comedy duo satirising racism while in blackface, have now been cut.

A BBC spokesman said in a statement: "This is a 20-year-old sketch show; in consultation with the programme makers, we have included the ones that still work today and not the ones that don't."

The Times reported the removed material included scenes featuring the English comic actors as war re-enactors in blackface, a sketch about a contestant on a makeover show wearing a burka and a "tribe" living in a garden centre.

BBC news has asked Mitchell and Webb - who rose to prominence on the Channel 4 sitcom Peep Show - for a comment.

That Mitchell and Webb Look grew out of a similar radio show titled That Mitchell and Webb Sound , which began on Radio 4 in 2003, and went on to win the Bafta for best comedy programme in 2007.

Defending the double act, fellow comedian Dom Joly, of Trigger Happy TV, questioned the BBC's "censorship" of itself.

Joly told The Times: "I totally get it if the BBC is putting out something really racist, which is laughing at and encouraging other people to feel that it's OK to do that.

"But it's so clear that Mitchell and Webb are not doing that. Their intent was not to be racist."

Jimmy Mulville, the co-founder of Hat Trick Productions, which makes the satirical news quiz Have I Got News For You, told the same newspaper he could understand the corporation's predicament.

"The BBC are in an impossible position," he said.

He added that producers had "to be careful", though, "that this is not the thin end of a wedge where we cut things out".

Perhaps Mitchell and Webb's best known sketch, which sees them both dressed as Nazis while begging the question: "are we the baddies?", remains online.

They are not the first comedians to have had their work edited or removed in recent years, as societal attitudes have shifted. Some artists themselves also began reassessing their work in the aftermath of the Black Lives Matter movement.

Matt Lucas and David Walliams' hit show Little Britain was removed from iPlayer, Netflix and BritBox in 2020, after objections resurfaced about some of their characters portraying people from different ethnic backgrounds.

At the time, both the BBC and Britbox noted how "times have changed" since the Little Britain first aired in the early noughties.

The show is now back on iPlayer but, like with Mitchell and Webb, some sketches have been removed.

articles.summary: US News: Patrick Clancy, the former husband of a US woman accused of killing their three children, has said he forgave her for their deaths, saying he would ha.
articles.body: Patrick Clancy, the former husband of a US woman accused of killing their three children, has said he forgave her for their deaths, saying he would have been “eaten up inside forever” if he had not.In an interview with CBS News, Clancy said he believed his former wife Lindsay Clancy’s severe mental illness was responsible for the killings. The BBC reported that Lindsay has not disputed that she killed the children, but her lawyers argued that she should not be held legally responsible because she was suffering from severe mental illness.Lindsay, now 36, was accused of strangling their children, Cora, 5, Dawson, 3, and Callan, 8 months, at their home in Duxbury, Massachusetts, on January 24, 2023. She later jumped from a second-floor window and was left paralysed.A judge declared a mistrial earlier this month after jurors failed to reach a unanimous verdict on whether Lindsay was criminally responsible for the killings. Prosecutors have not yet said whether they will seek a retrial.‘I believe mental illness caused it’Patrick said he had struggled to understand Lindsay’s condition in the months before the killings and admitted he “didn’t know how to manage a postpartum illness”.Lindsay’s defence team said she was suffering from postpartum psychosis, a rare condition that can involve severe disturbances in mood and thinking after childbirth.Patrick said he rejected descriptions of his former wife as a “killer mom” or “baby murderer”.“I believe that it was her mental illness that caused that,” he said, adding that forgiveness was necessary for him to cope with what happened.Asked whether he felt he had failed his family, Patrick said: “I think I did the best I could with what I had at the time. And I live with the outcome. I live with it every day.”Patrick faced online criticismPatrick also spoke about the intense online criticism and conspiracy theories surrounding the case, including claims that he was somehow responsible for the deaths of his children.He said the speculation was “deeply harmful to the legacy of my children” and distracted from what he believed was the key issue — perinatal mental health.Patrick has since found love again with Dr Rachel Danis. His remarriage became public in July 2026, when Lindsay’s attorney Kevin Reddington disclosed Patrick’s divorce from Lindsay and his new marriage ahead of her trial.Patrick said he experienced suicidal thoughts after the killings and eventually moved from Duxbury to New York City in search of anonymity.He and Danis are now building a family together, with Patrick saying he hopes to tell his future children about their three siblings.The case remains unresolved following the mistrial. articles.body: Human versus machine has moved a step closer to the fight cage. A six-foot-tall humanoid robot faced an influencer in San Francisco in a bout that the US robotics company REK called its first 'Human VS Terminator robot fight'.Footage shared by REK shows the influencer Frankie LaPenna facing the remotely controlled humanoid robot inside a cage in San Francisco. The event was organised as part of the company's work on a virtual reality combat game."We just made history with the first Human VS Terminator robot fight. Frankie LaPenna gave it his all," REK said in a caption accompanying the footage on X.The video shows the robot moving around the cage and warming up before the fight. Once the bout began, LaPenna threw several punches at the machine, which responded with punches and powerful kicks.At several points, the robot's kicks appeared to send LaPenna across the cage. The footage also shows him continuing to engage with the machine despite the force of the strikes.REK said the fight was part of its effort to develop a fast-paced virtual reality game where humans control humanoid robots in head-to-head battles. The company also said more footage from the match would be released.In a reply to a comment on X, REK's official account said LaPenna "kept going" and "defeated this robot."The footage quickly drew reactions online, with users speculating about whether human-controlled robots could eventually enter professional combat sports."Robots and humans fighting will be a part of the UFC in the next 5 years. AI hysteria demands it," one account said.Another user referenced the famous chess match between Garry Kasparov and IBM's Deep Blue, asking, "Is it too late to go back to Deep Blue beating Kasparov in chess only?""Terminator got his first practice," another person commented, while a separate user described the footage as a "dream coming true in real time".The incident is not the first humanoid-robot video to trigger Terminator comparisons. Earlier, footage from Saratov, Russia, showed a humanoid robot making erratic movements and attempting to kick a man after he appeared to push it at an electronics store. articles.title: Priscilla Chan's school project closed after 10 years and $125 million in funding, her organisation then committed another $10 million to support the surrounding community
articles.summary: US News: Priscilla Chan's education initiative, The Primary School, is closing after a decade of operations and reportedly more than $125 million in funding fr.
articles.body: Priscilla Chan's education initiative, The Primary School, is closing after a decade of operations and reportedly more than $125 million in funding from the Chan Zuckerberg Initiative (CZI). Founded to combine education with healthcare and family support, the project sought to address challenges affecting children's development and learning. Following the closure announcement, CZI committed more than $10 million towards community services in East Palo Alto and Belle Haven. The funding will support local healthcare, early childhood development and family wellbeing. The development highlights the challenges of sustaining privately funded education models and the role of philanthropy in supporting communities beyond individual schools.Priscilla Chan's school project and its $125 million fundingThe Primary School was established in 2016 with backing from Priscilla Chan and CZI. It sought to integrate classroom education with healthcare and family services, serving children in East Palo Alto, California, before expanding to San Leandro.The initiative was built on the idea that children's academic progress is influenced by their health, family circumstances and access to support. Its programme included educational instruction, healthcare, developmental screenings and parent wellness services.According to The Wall Street Journal, CZI provided more than $125 million to the school over approximately 10 years. The investment supported an ambitious model designed to address children's needs beyond traditional classroom teaching. However, the eventual closure prompted questions about educational outcomes and financial sustainability.Why The Primary School closedThe school's board announced that its East Palo Alto and San Leandro campuses would shut at the end of the 2025–2026 academic year. Funding challenges and questions surrounding the institution's future contributed to the decision.Coverage of the closure examined academic performance, leadership changes and the reliance on philanthropic backing. The Wall Street Journal also explored whether the school had achieved the educational outcomes expected from an initiative of its scale.Although the campuses are closing, some services developed through the project are being transferred to community organisations with support from CZI.An integrated approach to children's wellbeingThe Primary School brought together academic teaching, medical care and family assistance. Its model was intended to address circumstances that can influence a child's ability to learn and develop.Services included developmental screenings, healthcare and parent wellness coaching. Early intervention was another focus, with the aim of identifying children's needs during their formative years.This approach connected services that are often delivered by separate institutions. Its implementation also required coordination between educators, healthcare professionals and families.CZI announces more than $10 million in community investmentOn April 13, 2026, CZI announced more than $10 million in grants and investments for East Palo Alto and Belle Haven. The funding is intended to strengthen healthcare, early childhood development and family wellness programmes.The announcement forms part of a broader $50 million commitment made in 2025 to support local communities. The organisation is working with established service providers rather than directing all its funding towards a single educational institution.This strategy aims to maintain access to essential services through organisations already operating in the area.Three organisations receive $7 millionThe official announcement identified three recipients of a combined $7 million in grants.Children's Health Council: $3 millionThe funding will support the adaptation and continuation of The Primary School's Parent Wellness Coaching programme.Ravenswood Family Health Network: $3 millionThe grant will help expand school-based physical and behavioural healthcare across East Palo Alto and Belle Haven.Ravenswood Early Learning: $1 millionThe organisation will launch an early intervention initiative for children aged zero to five, including developmental screening, referrals and follow-up services.These grants account for $7 million of the announced investment. CZI describes the wider package as exceeding $10 million, with the remaining funding not fully itemised through these three grants.Support for students and familiesThe closure required families to consider alternative schools and healthcare providers. Some parents had relied on the institution for integrated services alongside education.The San Francisco Chronicle reported in April 2025 that transition assistance included financial support for families across different age groups.CZI also said it provided bridge funding to help students move into the Ravenswood City School District. Discussions about possible affordable housing investments for teachers and staff have formed part of its wider engagement with the district.Separately, CZI announced $3.6 million in education savings accounts for nearly 550 students at The Primary School across East Palo Alto and the East Bay. The accounts are designed to assist families with future education expenses.The future of philanthropic educationThe Primary School's closure raises questions about how education initiatives funded by private philanthropy can sustain their operations and demonstrate results over time.Its experience brings together several issues, including academic achievement, institutional leadership, financial continuity and the delivery of integrated services.CZI's community funding represents a continuation of support for healthcare, early learning and family wellbeing, even though the school's campuses are closing. The effectiveness of these programmes will depend on their implementation, reach and ability to provide consistent assistance to local residents.The transition marks a change in how CZI supports education and community development in East Palo Alto and Belle Haven.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Google fined €403m by Irish data watchdog over location tracking
articles.summary: The penalty follows an inquiry launched into the tech giant six years ago, following complaints from several European consumer rights organisations.
articles.body:
Google has been fined €403m (£345m) by the Republic of Ireland's Data Protection Commission (DPC) over its handling of location data.

The penalty - one of the largest of its kind imposed by the Irish watchdog authority - followed an inquiry launched into the tech giant six years ago, following complaints from several European consumer rights organisations.

On Monday the DPC said its investigation found Google had processed data in a manner that was not "lawful", "fair" or "transparent".

The inquiry concerned Google's processing of location data in three specific features - Web & App Activity, Location History and Location Accuracy between 25 May 2018 to 4 February 2020.

Location data is any kind of data which can be used to infer a person's location.

It can "reveal a significant amount of information about an individual, including information that is inherently private", said DPC deputy commissioner Graham Doyle in a statement released on Monday.

The report said Google's practices "infringed" General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) - legislation that came into effect on 25 May, 2018, creating strict data privacy and security law within the European Union (EU).

Doyle added: "The GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation) provides a high level of protection of personal data throughout the EEA (European Economic Area), and requires that the processing of personal data must be carried out in a lawful, fair and transparent manner."

He continued: "As a result of Google's failures... individuals could have been unaware that their location was being used to, for example, influence them with ads or to infer their interests, and could lose control over their personal data.

"The retention of users' location data for longer than necessary aggravated this loss of control."

In addition to being fined, Google has also been ordered to bring its data processing into compliance within six months.

In a statement, Google said: "This case centres around historical policies that have since been updated. From 2019 onwards, we've significantly evolved our practices and launched robust tools that make managing location data simple."

They also said they have made data protection improvements in recent years, including "industry-first auto-delete controls", which enables all users to "set your account to automatically delete your data on a rolling three, 18, or 36-month basis".

Other measures to safeguard personal data have also been introduced, they said, such as "simple ads management", which allows you "to turn off personalized ads entirely", and "increased transparency", including "consolidated detailed information about our location data practices and account settings".

articles.title: Xi's 'anti-graft' crackdown continues: Two senior generals expelled from CCP, Chinese military
articles.summary: China News: The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has expelled two senior officers from the party and the armed forces over \"economic wrongdoing\" and “serious violati.
articles.body: The Chinese Communist Party (CCP) has expelled two senior officers from the party and the armed forces over "economic wrongdoing" and “serious violations of discipline and law," state-run Xinhua news agency reported on Monday.Zhang Youxia, a vice-chairman of the Central Military Commission (CMC), the CCP’s top military command body, was second-in-command under President Xi Jinping and has long been regarded as one of his closest military allies. Liu Zhenli was also a CMC member and headed its Joint Staff Department.Investigations against Zhang and Liu were announced in January, and both were removed from the state Central Military Commission in late August.The CCP leadership accused the two officers of “disloyalty, corruption, dereliction of duty” and other serious disciplinary violations.Zhang and Liu “seriously violated political discipline and political rules, formed cliques and factions, and were disloyal and dishonest to the party”, Xinhua cited official documents as saying.The two “crossed red lines and basic limits”, the documents said, adding that their “political and economic wrongdoing were intertwined, and "corrupt self-enrichment" coexisted with dereliction of duty and abuse of office”.“The sums involved were exceptionally large; the nature (of their conduct) was extremely serious and the impact extremely egregious,” it said.Zhang was also a member of the ruling Communist Party’s elite Politburo and was among the few senior Chinese military officers with combat experience.Chinese military a major target of Xi's 'anti-corruption' crackdownThe Chinese military has been a major target of a broader anti-corruption campaign launched by Xi after he became president in 2013.In August, General Zhao Zongqi, who commanded the People’s Liberation Army’s (PLA) Western Theatre Command during the 2017 Doklam standoff and the 2020 Galwan Valley clash with India, was sacked from Beijing’s top political advisory body. No reason was given for his removal, and no investigation against him was announced.In October 2025, nine senior generals were expelled from the CCP and military for “seriously violating party discipline” and showing a “total collapse of beliefs."In December last year, China’s parliament removed three senior military officials as part of a broader “anti-corruption crackdown."(With Reuters inputs)Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
